operations.specification: Create a new cart item by validating that the provided variantId exists and is active, has sufficient stock (stock > 0), belongs to an approved seller (approval_status = 'approved'), and the product has not been deleted. Capture and store exact snapshot values from the product, variant, and seller at the time of addition: product name, product description, variant option values, variant price, seller shop name, and seller logo. Insert new record with quantity = 1, created_at and updated_at set to current timestamp, and deleted_at = null. Return the complete cart item object with all snapshot fields to the client. Validate that the customer_id in context matches the authenticated user. Return 400 if variant not found, 400 if stock insufficient, 400 if seller not approved, 400 if product is deleted.
operations.description:
Add a specific product variant to the customer's shopping cart while capturing an immutable snapshot of the product's exact state at the time of addition.

This operation ensures pricing and product description integrity by preserving the product name, description, variant options, variant price, seller shop name, and seller logo exactly as they appeared when the customer added the item to their cart. This prevents sellers from manipulating product pricing, descriptions, or profiles after the fact and ensures that when a customer proceeds to checkout, the price and product details they see in their cart are identical to what was available when they added the item.

The snapshots are critical for dispute resolution. If a customer claims they purchased a product with specific characteristics (color, size, price, seller branding) and the product has since been modified, the snapshot recorded at cart addition provides definitive proof of what was offered at time of purchase.

This operation directly maps to the shopping_mall_cart_items table, persisting the exact values from snapshot_product_name, snapshot_product_description, snapshot_variant_options, snapshot_variant_price, snapshot_seller_shop_name, and snapshot_seller_logo as defined by the database schema.

The operation returns the full cart item object including all snapshot fields so the client can immediately display accurate information to the customer without requiring additional queries.

This operation references assets from shopping_mall_product_variants table (for variant_id and stock), shopping_mall_products table (for name and description), and shopping_mall_sellers table (for shop_name and logo). Prior to cart addition, the system must validate that the variant is active (deleted_at = null), has sufficient stock, and the seller is approved (approval_status = 'approved').

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new cart item with immutable product and seller snapshots.

responseBody.description: The newly created cart item with all snapshot data preserved at time of addition.

operations.name: create

operations.description:
Remove a specific cart item from the customer's active shopping cart by its unique identifier. This operation performs a logical deletion on the shopping_mall_cart_items table by setting the deleted_at timestamp, preserving the cart item data for audit and historical purposes while removing it from active cart consideration. The cart item is identified by its unique UUID in the path parameter.

This operation aligns with the snapshot principle where cart items are never physically deleted from the system, as they serve as critical audit records for pricing integrity, dispute resolution, and financial reporting. The cart item data remains accessible through the shopping_mall_cart_items table for historical analysis, but is excluded from active cart calculations and checkout operations.

Authorization: Only the customer who owns the cart item may remove it. Customers cannot delete other customers' cart items. The system validates that the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer before deletion.

Relationship to other operations: This operation is complementary to the cart addition and quantity modification operations. After successful deletion, the cart total is recalculated automatically. If the customer wishes to restore the item, they must re-add it through the cart addition operation.

Error handling: If the cart item does not exist, a 404 error is returned. If the cart item belongs to another customer, a 403 error is returned. If the cart item is already deleted, a 410 error is returned.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Execute a logical deletion of a cart item by updating the shopping_mall_cart_items record to set the deleted_at timestamp to the current UTC time, where the id matches the cartItemId path parameter and the customer_id matches the authenticated user's ID. Use database transaction to ensure atomicity. Validate before deletion: 1) cart item with specified id exists 2) cart item belongs to the authenticated customer 3) cart item is not already deleted (deleted_at is null). If any validation fails, return appropriate error code without modifying database. If successful, return 204 No Content. Do not physically delete the record from the database to preserve audit trail as required by the snapshot principle.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of your order history.

This operation enables customers to view their personal order history with advanced filtering options including order status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), date range filtering, and total amount thresholds. The response returns paginated summary data optimized for list displays rather than full order details, improving performance for large result sets. Each summary includes essential information such as order number, total amount, status, creation date, and order item count, with full order details available via the GET /shopping_mall/customer/orders/{orderId} endpoint.

Filtering supports complex combinations: search for all paid orders in the last 90 days, or orders with total amount greater than $50. Date ranges can be specified as start/end dates or relative periods (last 7 days, this month, etc.). Order totals can be filtered using comparison operators (greater than, less than, between). For performance reasons, only the most relevant order summary data is returned, reducing payload size and improving response times.

This endpoint is designed to handle large datasets efficiently through offset/limit pagination, with support for sorting by any field (created_at, total_amount, status). Search filters are case-insensitive for text fields and exact matches for status codes. Results are automatically filtered to the authenticated customer's own orders only.

Related operations: GET /shopping_mall/customer/orders/{orderId} to retrieve full details of a specific order, GET /shopping_mall/customer/orders/{orderId}/items to list all items in a specific order.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_orders table with pagination and comprehensive filtering.

Apply filters for status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), creation date range (start/end), customer_id, seller_id, and total_amount (with comparison operators: >, <, >=, <=, between).

For customer requests, automatically filter by customer_id from JWT token.

For admin requests, allow filtering across all customers and sellers.

Support sorting by: created_at (asc/desc), total_amount (asc/desc), status (alphabetically).

Implement cursor-based pagination: use offset/limit for small datasets, cursor-based for large datasets with >1000 records.

Return only the summary fields: id, order_number, status, total_amount, created_at, customer_id, customer_email, order_item_count.

Do not join order_items table in primary query - use subqueries or cached counts for performance.

Handle empty or malformed filters gracefully by returning empty results.

Log all search parameters for analytics and audit purposes.

Apply rate limiting: 100 requests per minute per user.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summaries optimized for display

Include all snapshot fields from order_items: product_name, product_description, category_name, base_price, thumbnail_image, all_product_images, variant_sku, option_values, variant_price, stock_at_time_of_purchase, shop_name, shop_description, logo_url. Filter by order_id and ensure deleted_at is null. Return order header fields: order_number, status, total_amount, created_at, updated_at. All data must reflect the state at time of purchase, not current data. No caching allowed. Use database transaction for consistency.
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a specific order by its unique identifier.

This operation returns a comprehensive view of a customer's order, including all items purchased with their exact state at the time of purchase, preserving product specifications, pricing, and seller identity as immutable snapshots for audit and dispute resolution. This table serves as the immutable audit trail for all commercial transactions, preserving pricing, product details, and seller identity even if those details change later. Required for dispute resolution, financial reporting, and legal compliance. All data is frozen at checkout and never altered.

The order head record captures the immutable state of the order at time of payment confirmation, including the customer's selected shipping address and the exact order status derived from its constituent order items. This ensures complete auditability and provides irrefutable evidence for dispute resolution and legal compliance.

For each order item, the response includes the exact product name, description, category, and base price as they existed when the order was placed, regardless of any subsequent changes. Variant-specific details including SKU, option values (e.g., color, size), unit price, and stock quantity are preserved in their exact historical state. Seller information including shop name, description, and logo are captured as they appeared at purchase time to maintain brand integrity and reputation context.

The order header provides meta-information including order number, status, total amount, and creation/update timestamps. This operation is critical for customer self-service, enabling users to verify their purchase history with complete fidelity to the state of the marketplace at the time of transaction.

This endpoint is exclusively available to the authenticated customer who placed the order, or to platform administrators with elevated privileges for dispute resolution and oversight purposes.

Note: No other API operations need to be pre-executed to access this data. All information is fully contained within the order and its associated order items.

parameters.name: orderId

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of order items associated with a specific order.

This operation provides comprehensive access to all order items linked to a given order, permitting filtering by item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), sorting by creation date or total amount, and pagination for large result sets. The data returned is sourced entirely from immutable snapshots embedded within order_items, ensuring that pricing, product descriptions, variant options, and seller profiles are displayed exactly as they existed at time of purchase. No live data or current states are used - every field in the response reflects the frozen snapshot state at checkout.

The endpoint enforces strict access control: customers can only access their own order's items, sellers can only access items where their seller_id matches, and administrators have full view across all orders. Order items cannot be modified, edited, or deleted; this endpoint is strictly read-only to preserve the forensic integrity of transaction history as mandated by the snapshot principle in 12-snapshot-principle.md.

This endpoint interacts with shopping_mall_order_items, leveraging the snapshot_data JSONB field to reconstruct historical product and seller state. It does not join with live products, variants, or sellers - those references exist only for historical context, not current state. Status transitions (paid → shipped → delivered) are automatically derived from item-level transitions and reflected in the order's overall status as per 07-order-management.md.

Critical patterns:
- All product_name, product_description, variant_sku, and shop_name fields in the response are snapshot values from the time of purchase
- No dynamic price calculation - unit_price is immutable from snapshot
- All pagination uses cursor-based (after/before) rather than offset-based to handle large datasets efficiently
- Requests do not perform any filtering on computed fields (e.g., total_amount) but only on stored snapshot values

External dependencies:
- Must validate that requested orderId exists and user has permission to view
- Must ensure no snapshot data is altered by any internal logic
- Must not expose any raw database fields (e.g., created_at)
- Must return snapshot data, not live records

For consistency: All operations should always treat order items as historical records - never as editable entities.

Implement cursor-based pagination with after/before parameters to handle large result sets. For each result, include: product_name, product_description, category_name, base_price, thumbnail_image, all_product_images, variant_sku, option_values, variant_price, stock_at_time_of_purchase, shop_name, shop_description, logo_url, quantity, unit_price, item_total, status, created_at, updated_at. Do NOT join with live product, variant, or seller tables - use ONLY snapshot data. Return total record count for pagination metadata. Log access for audit trail per 07-order-management.md.

Retrieve a specific order item with complete snapshot data as it existed at the time of purchase.

This endpoint provides the exact state of a product variant, including product details, pricing, and seller identity, as they existed at the moment of purchase. This immutable snapshot is critical for dispute resolution, financial auditing, and legal compliance, as it preserves the complete transaction context even if product details, pricing, or seller profiles have changed since the purchase.

The response includes all fields from the order item snapshot: product name and description, category information, base price, product images, variant SKU and option values, variant price, stock quantity at time of purchase, seller shop name, description, and logo. This ensures customers and administrators can verify exactly what was purchased and under what conditions.

All data is retrieved directly from the shopping_mall_order_items table which stores complete snapshots of every transaction. The snapshot fields are maintained as immutable records and are never updated after creation.

Authentication: Customers can access their own order items. Administrators can access any order item on the platform.

Related endpoints: GET /orders/{orderId} (retrieves entire order), PATCH /orders (searches all order items), GET /shopping_mall_products/{productId} (retrieves current product state, which may differ from snapshot).

operations.description:
Create a new shipment record for a single order item. This operation initiates the physical delivery process by recording the carrier and tracking information, and transitions the associated order item status from 'paid' to 'shipped'.

Each shipment is linked to exactly one order item and must be created by the seller who fulfilled that item. This ensures proper accountability and prevents cross-seller shipment bundling, which would violate the platform's business rules.

The system requires the carrier name and tracking number to be provided, creating a permanent record of the delivery logistics at the time of shipment. Once created, the shipment record cannot be altered, deleted, or modified in any way. The system automatically transitions the associated order item to 'delivered' after 14 days if the customer does not manually confirm delivery, as defined in the platform's delivery policy.

This operation triggers the creation of immutable snapshots preserving the exact state of:
- The seller's profile (shop name, description, logo)
- The product (name, description, images, category)
- The product variant (SKU, option values, price, stock quantity at time of shipment)

These snapshots are preserved for the lifetime of the platform, enabling complete dispute resolution and audit trail integrity regardless of future changes to products or seller profiles.

This operation must be called after the seller has prepared the physical package and is ready to hand it over to the carrier. The tracking number must be the actual carrier-provided identifier, not a placeholder or dummy value.

Related Operations:
- GET /orders/{orderId}/items - To view which order items are eligible for shipment (status: 'paid')
- POST /orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}/confirm-delivery - For customer to manually confirm delivery
- GET /shipments - To view all shipment records for audit purposes

Important: No shipment can contain items from multiple sellers. Each shipment must reference exactly one order item belonging to a single seller.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shipment record for an order item with status 'paid'.

1. Validate order item exists and has status 'paid' using {orderItemId} path parameter
2. Verify order item belongs to the authenticated seller
3. Validate carrier name is non-empty and ≤100 characters
4. Validate tracking number is alphanumeric and 8-32 characters
5. Create shipment record with provided data
6. Set status to 'shipped'
7. Set created_at to current timestamp
8. Associate the shipment with the given order item
9. Update the associated order item's status from 'paid' to 'shipped'
10. Return the created shipment record with full details

Edge cases:
- If order item status is not 'paid', return 400
- If carrier name is empty or exceeds 100 characters, return 400
- If tracking number is empty, contains non-alphanumeric characters, or is not 8-32 chars, return 400
- If order item is not owned by authenticated seller, return 403
- If order item is already shipped, return 409

Transaction must be atomic - if any validation fails, rollback all changes.

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment record with all details

If system triggers after 14 days, transition status to 'auto-delivered' without reason. For customer-initiated delivery confirmation, verify customer owns this shipment. For system-triggered delivery, verify 14 days have passed since shipment creation. Create immutable shipment status change record with timestamp and actor (customer or system). Return 400 if status is already 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered'. Return 404 if shipment does not exist or is not in 'shipped' status.
operations.description:
Initiate delivery status confirmation for a shipment, either through customer action or system automation.

This operation allows a customer to explicitly confirm delivery of their shipment, or triggers automatic delivery confirmation after 14 days of the shipment being marked as 'shipped'. The system enforces immutable status transitions: once a shipment is marked as 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered', it cannot be reverted.

For customer-initiated delivery confirmation, the customer must provide a reason for delivery, which is permanently stored as part of the audit trail. This provides accountability and context for the delivery event. For automatic delivery, the system performs the transition without user input after the 14-day period expires, ensuring business continuity even when customers do not respond. Both transitions create permanent, unalterable records in the shipment status history.

This operation is critical for inventory restoration workflows: when a shipment is confirmed delivered, the system automatically restores the inventory of the associated product variants. The operation's immutability ensures that delivery status cannot be manipulated after the fact, preserving the integrity of financial reconciliation and dispute resolution processes. It also directly connects to the order management system, where the delivery confirmation triggers eligibility for customer reviews and ratings.

The customer must own the shipment being confirmed. System automation only initiates delivery confirmation when the shipment has been in 'shipped' status for 14 days, calculated from the shipment creation timestamp, not the estimated delivery date. Both delivery methods preserve the exact state of the shipment at time of transition in the immutable shopping_mall_shipments table, ensuring complete auditability.

This operation is directly linked to the order item status logic described in 07-order-management.md, where delivery confirmation causes the associated order item to transition from 'shipped' to 'delivered'. This synchronization ensures consistent status across all related business entities within the shoppingMall ecosystem.

Authorized actors include customers who placed the order and sellers who created the shipment, who can track delivery progress using the provided tracking number. operations.name: at

operations.description:
Initiate a cancellation request for a paid order item.

This operation allows customers to formally request cancellation of an order item that has been paid for but not yet shipped. Customers must provide a detailed reason (10-500 characters) explaining why they wish to cancel the item. The system automatically identifies the customer from the order item context and sets the request status to 'pending'. The reason provided by the customer is stored and made available to the seller for response. This creates an immutable record of the customer's justification for cancellation, which is critical for dispute resolution and platform integrity.

The endpoint does not return any response body because cancellation request creation is a stateless operation that only modifies the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table. Success is indicated by HTTP 201 Created status, and failures (such as invalid order item status or missing reason) are communicated through appropriate HTTP error codes (400 Bad Request).

A successful cancellation request triggers two system events: The cancellation_request record is created, and a notification is sent to the associated seller. This follows the platform's snapshot principle - the exact reason, timestamp, and context at the time of request creation are preserved permanently.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that order_item_id refers to an existing order item with status 'paid'. Verify reason is 10-500 characters and not empty. Extract customer_id from the order_item's related customer through database join. Create new cancellation_requests record with status='pending', created_at=now(), updated_at=now(), auto_approve_at=now() + 48 hours. Log the request in system_logs with actor=customer_id and action='create_cancellation_request'. Return HTTP 201 Created with no response body. If order item status is not 'paid', return HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Cannot cancel items that are not in paid status'. If reason is missing or invalid length, return HTTP 400 Bad Request with message 'Reason must be between 10 and 500 characters'.

requestBody.description: Request payload for creating a new cancellation request

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table with filters for status, customer_id, order_item_id, created_at range, and auto_approve_at range. Return paginated results with cursor-based pagination. Join with shopping_mall_order_items and shopping_mall_customers to include order item details and customer display names where needed. Apply sorting by created_at descending. Include only records where auto_approve_at > now() or status != 'pending' to handle both pending and non-pending requests efficiently. Validate that request body filters are within allowed fields only.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of cancellation requests for order items.

This operation enables customers and administrators to search through cancellation requests with complex criteria including status (pending, approved, rejected), associated customer, order item, and creation date range. Each request represents a customer-initiated effort to cancel a paid order item that has not yet been shipped, following the 48-hour auto-approval workflow defined in the business requirements.

The response includes summary information for each cancellation request, optimized for list display while preserving critical context such as reason, status, and auto-approval deadline. This endpoint is essential for monitoring pending requests, identifying auto-approved cancellations, and handling administrative disputes.

All queries are performed using the request body with structured filtering parameters. This design follows the standard pattern for complex list operations in the platform, ensuring consistent API behavior across all search endpoints. Note that cancellation requests are immutable records preserved for audit purposes, and this endpoint provides read-only access to historical request data.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete details of a specific cancellation request made by a customer.

This endpoint returns the full state of a cancellation request identified by its unique requestId. The response includes the cancellation reason provided by the customer, the current status (always 'pending' until resolved), the exact time the request was created, and the system-generated timestamp when it will be automatically approved if no seller responds.

The endpoint enforces strict ownership validation: only the customer who initiated the request (via the associated order item) or an administrator can access this information. The data returned is immutable and reflects the exact state of the request at the moment of retrieval, preserving the context for dispute resolution.

Cancellation requests are only created for order items with status 'paid'. Once submitted, the request triggers a 48-hour auto-approval countdown. This endpoint allows customers to track whether their request is still pending or has been automatically approved. Administrators can use this data for audit purposes and to identify potential seller inactivity patterns.

For security, all requests are validated against the authenticated user's identity. The requestId parameter corresponds to the primary key in the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table. This operation does not allow changing the request state - modifications can only be triggered by a seller's response or the auto-approval system.

Validate that the shopping_mall_customer_id matches the customer who placed the original order. Create a new refund request entry with status 'pending', the provided reason, and the auto_approval_deadline set to 72 hours from current time. Return the created refund request object with assigned ID and generated timestamps.
operations.description:
Initiate a refund request for a delivered order item.

Customers may request a refund for any order item with status 'delivered' within a 7-day window from the delivery date. This endpoint allows customers to submit a refund request by providing a reason for the refund, which will be reviewed by the seller. The system automatically approves the refund if the seller does not respond within 72 hours.

This operation is essential for customer protection and ensures fair resolution of post-purchase issues. The refund request must be associated with a specific delivered order item, and the customer must provide a reason for the refund that is between 10 and 500 characters long.

This operation directly interacts with the shopping_mall_refund_requests database table, which has the following constraints:
- Must reference a valid shopping_mall_order_item_id with status 'delivered'
- Must reference the customer_id who placed the original order
- reason field must be 10-500 characters long
- initial status is 'pending'
- auto_approval_deadline is set 72 hours from created_at

Only the customer who originally purchased the item may submit a refund request for that item. Duplicate refund requests for the same order item are prohibited by the @@unique([shopping_mall_order_item_id]) constraint on the shopping_mall_refund_requests table. The refund request system preserves all historical context to ensure accurate dispute resolution.

requestBody.description: Details required to create a new refund request

responseBody.description: The created refund request with assigned identifiers and timestamps

prerequisites.description: Shipment must be created for the order item to transition from 'paid' status to 'shipped' and eventually to 'delivered', which is required before a refund request can be initiated.

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_refund_requests table with filtering by status, customer_id, created_at date range, and reason keyword search. Apply pagination with cursor-based pagination for scalable results. Join with shopping_mall_customers to include customer name (or 'deleted user' if account deleted). Join with shopping_mall_order_items to include order number and product information. Filter to only return refund requests with deleted_at IS NULL. Return count of total matching records and pagination metadata. Implement indexing on status, created_at, and reason for performance optimization.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of refund requests filtered by various criteria.

This endpoint allows authorized users to search for refund requests using status filters, date ranges, customer identifiers, and keyword searches on refund reasons. The endpoint is essential for customer service, seller dispute resolution, and administrative oversight in a marketplace with high volumes of transactions where immutable data records must be easily retrievable.

The operation supports comprehensive search functionality including filtering by refund request status ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected'), date range for when the request was created, specific customer identifier, and keyword matching in the refund reason text. Results are returned in paginated format to handle large datasets efficiently.

This endpoint is designed to complement the immutable snapshot architecture of the platform, providing rapid access to refund request history while respecting the principle that all records are preserved indefinitely. The search functionality operates on the current state of refund requests, not on snapshots, as requests can still be in 'pending' status and subject to change.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for refund requests

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request summaries

operations.name: patch

operations.specification: Retrieve a single refund request by its unique ID from the shopping_mall_refund_requests table. Perform authorization check to ensure requester is either the original customer who submitted the request or an administrator. Return the complete refund request object including id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, shopping_mall_customer_id, reason, status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, and auto_approval_deadline. Handle case where request ID does not exist or is not accessible due to permissions by returning 404. Ensure no data exposure occurs for refund requests not associated with the requester. No database joins or external services required for this operation.
operations.description:
Retrieve the details of a specific refund request by its unique identifier.

This API endpoint returns comprehensive information about a customer-initiated refund request for an order item with status 'delivered'. The refund request captures the customer's reason for requesting a refund, the status of the request (pending, approved, or rejected), and the automatic approval deadline.

This endpoint is used by customers to review their own refund requests and by administrators to inspect refund request details during dispute resolution. The data provided here includes the exact reason text submitted by the customer, the current status of the request, and the timestamp when the system will automatically approve the request if the seller does not respond within 72 hours.

The request ID is a unique UUID that identifies the specific refund request, and access is strictly controlled by authorization rules that prevent unauthorized access to refund requests not associated with the current user.

Records may be soft deleted by administrators for compliance or system integrity reasons. When a refund request is soft deleted, it is marked with a deleted_at timestamp and is no longer accessible via this endpoint unless requested by an administrator with appropriate permissions.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the refund request. This is the UUID primary key of the shopping_mall_refund_requests record.

responseBody.description: The complete refund request record including all details as they existed when the request was created.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Submit a final, immutable response to a customer-initiated cancellation request.

This operation allows a seller to respond to a pending cancellation request by either approving or rejecting it. The response is permanently recorded in the system as an immutable audit record for dispute resolution. When approved, the system automatically restores the inventory quantity of the associated product variant and changes the order item status to "cancelled". When rejected, the cancellation request closes and the order item remains as paid.

The seller must provide one mandatory field: "decision" — which must be exactly "approve" or "reject". If the decision is "reject", the seller must also provide a reason with 10–500 characters to explain the refusal. The reason field is ignored if response is "approve".

The cancellation_request_id in the path parameter is linked to a single, verified order item that was purchased by the customer who requested cancellation. Only the seller who created the associated product can respond to this request. The operation validates the seller’s authorization against the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.seller_id derived from order_item. This endpoint does not support bulk operations, conditional answers, or retries — it creates exactly one immutable response record.

All responses are permanently recorded in the shopping_mall_request_responses table with timestamped audit data. Administrators can view all responses in the admin dashboard for compliance and oversight. No customer can edit or cancel a response — only the seller can submit one, and only once.

This endpoint is extensionally linked to 09-cancellation-refund.md which mandates the 48-hour auto-approval window for unanswered requests. If no response is submitted by the seller within 48 hours, the system automatically approves the cancellation. This endpoint allows the seller to respond ahead of time and override automatic approval.

The purchase status of the associated order item and the inventory history are updated as a direct consequence of this response. The customer is notified of the outcome via push notification and email. If approved, the customer is issued a refund automatically.

This endpoint depends on the previously established workflow of cancellation request submission — customers cannot request cancellation unless the order item status is "paid" and has not yet been shipped.
operations.name: respond
operations.specification: Fetch the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests record using the requestId path parameter. Validate that the record exists and has status 'pending'. Validate that the requester is not already approved or rejected. Validate that the authenticated seller has access to this request (seller_id matches the request's order_item's seller_id). If decision is 'reject', validate that reason is 10-500 characters. If decision is 'approve', validate that reason is null. Create a new shopping_mall_request_responses record with decision, reason, seller_id, and created_at. Update the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests record status to match decision ('approved' or 'rejected'). If response is approve, trigger inventory restoration: create a positive inventory_history entry for the variant with reason 'cancellation approved'. Trigger order item status update: update corresponding shopping_mall_order_items status to 'cancelled'. Record response snapshot in shopping_mall_refund_response_snapshots (as this is the same schema used for refund responses due to identical structure). Return the full created shopping_mall_request_responses record with timestamp and resolved status. All operations must be wrapped in a single database transaction to ensure consistency.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the cancellation request being responded to. This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table. Must be a UUID.
parameters.name: requestId

requestBody.description: The seller's response to the cancellation request, containing decision and optional reason.

responseBody.description: The created immutable response record, including decision, reason, and timestamp.

operations.description:
Respond to a customer-initiated refund request for an order item.

This operation allows a seller to approve or reject a refund request submitted by a customer for a specific order item. When a customer requests a refund for a delivered product, a refund request is created in the system with status 'pending'. The seller must respond to this request within 72 hours, or the system will automatically approve it. This endpoint enables the seller to provide a decision ('approve' or 'reject') along with a reason (minimum 10 characters, maximum 500 characters). The response is stored as an immutable record that cannot be modified or deleted, preserving the exact decision and reason as it was submitted.

The refund request is linked to an order item, which contains the exact product state, variant configuration, seller profile, and price as they existed at time of purchase. This operation preserves this context by tying the seller's response to the specific refund request. Upon successful response, the refund request status is updated to match the seller's decision, and an immutable audit record is created in the system for audit purposes.

This operation is only allowed for sellers who are the owners of the product associated with the refund request. The seller's response is final and cannot be changed after submission. If the seller rejects the request, the customer may not submit another refund request for the same order item. If the seller approves the request, the system will restore inventory to the product variant and process the financial refund according to the platform refund policy.

The response reason must be provided by the seller and must be at least 10 characters in length, with a maximum of 500 characters. This ensures accountability and provides meaningful context for customers and administrators in case of disputes. The response timestamp is recorded precisely when the seller submits it, and this cannot be altered or falsified.

This operation is governed by strict audit trail requirements: every response creation event is recorded in the system's immutable audit history, and administrators have access to all response histories for dispute resolution. These records are preserved indefinitely and are used as authoritative records for resolving commercial disputes, compliance audits, and fraud investigations.

For security and access control: Only authenticated sellers who are the owners of the product associated with the refund request may call this endpoint. This endpoint does not allow customer-initiated responses or responses from non-owner sellers. Attempting to respond to a refund request owned by another seller will result in a 403 Forbidden response.

This operation does not create or modify any order items, shipping records, or inventory records directly. These changes occur through separate business processes triggered by the response status change. The API operation is strictly limited to capturing the seller's decision and reason as an immutable audit record.

This endpoint is designed to work in conjunction with the system's auto-approval feature: if no response is received within 72 hours of the refund request being created, the system will automatically approve the refund without requiring any manual intervention from the seller. Manual responses, however, override the automatic approval process and are recorded with their exact submission timestamp for audit completeness.
operations.name: approveRefund
operations.specification: Find refund request by ID in shopping_mall_refund_requests table using requestId path parameter. Validate seller has ownership of the product linked to this refund request by joining with shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_sellers. Validate seller is authenticated and matches seller_id on the refund request. Validate that the refund request status is currently 'pending'. Extract decision (must be 'approve' or 'reject') and reason (10-500 characters) from request body. Create new shopping_mall_refund_response_snapshots record with refund_request_id, seller_id, decision, reason, and current timestamp. Update the shopping_mall_refund_requests status field to match the decision provided. Return HTTP 201 Created with the created response snapshot. If refund request not found, return 404. If seller is unauthorized (not owner of product), return 403. If refund request is not 'pending', return 409 Conflict. If decision is not 'approve' or 'reject', return 400 Bad Request. If reason is below 10 or above 500 characters, return 400 Bad Request. Ensure all operations are in a single atomic transaction to prevent inconsistent states. All data in response snapshot must be immutable. Never allow deletion or modification of response snapshot after creation.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the refund request being responded to. This links to the shopping_mall_refund_requests table.
parameters.name: requestId

requestBody.description: Contains the seller's decision and reason for the refund request response.

responseBody.description: The immutable snapshot record of the seller's response to the refund request including decision, reason, and timestamp.

prerequisites.description: Refund request must be created before a seller can respond to it
Order item must be shipped (via shipment creation) to reach 'delivered' status before refund request can be initiated

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_reviews table with pagination and multiple filter criteria. Support filtering by product_id, customer_id, rating range (min/max), created_at date range, updated_at date range, text search term (using full-text search on text column), and deleted_at status. Apply pagination with cursor-based pagination for performance on large datasets. Include only records where deleted_at is null (active reviews) unless specifically filtering for deleted reviews. Join with shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_customers to include product name and customer display name in summary response. When text search is provided, use GIN trigram index on text field for efficient partial matching. Apply rating range filter for 1-5 scale. Return results sorted by created_at descending (newest first) by default, with ability to sort by rating or updated_at. Include total count of matching reviews in pagination metadata.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of customer reviews for products.

This operation allows users to search for reviews across the entire platform using multiple criteria including product, customer, rating, date range, and text content. It is the primary endpoint for discovering customer feedback on products and for administrators to monitor review quality and authenticity.

The search supports comprehensive filtering capabilities: you can filter by specific product (using product ID), specific customer (using customer ID), rating range (1-5 stars), creation date range, last update date range, and partial text matching within review content using full-text search. By default, only active (not deleted) reviews are returned, but you can also search for deleted reviews by specifying appropriate criteria.

Results are returned with pagination, including metadata about total results and pagination state, allowing efficient navigation through large datasets. The summary response includes essential information about each review: its rating, partial text content, product and customer identifiers, and timestamps, optimized for display in review lists.

This endpoint is used by customers browsing products to read relevant reviews, by sellers analyzing customer feedback on their products, and by administrators conducting review audits or investigating potential review manipulation.

To ensure data integrity and preserve historical context, this search only returns reviews whose current state matches the search criteria. For full review history including edits and deletions, use the review snapshots endpoint. All filter combinations are supported, and results are sorted by creation date in descending order (newest first) unless otherwise specified.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering reviews.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summaries with metadata.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_reviews table by reviewId to get current review state. Join with shopping_mall_review_snapshots table to retrieve all historical snapshots of this review. Return current review with status (active, deleted) and array of snapshots ordered by created_at descending. Ensure that when review.deleted_at is not null, the review is marked as deleted but still returned with snapshot history. Do not use soft delete keywords unless implementing soft deletion, but here we are using deleted_at field as per schema.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific customer review and its complete historical snapshot history.

This operation returns the current state of a customer review along with all previous versions captured in snapshots. The review can be active, edited, or deleted, and the response includes the complete history of changes to provide full context for dispute resolution.

When a review is edited, the previous version is preserved as a snapshot capturing the rating, text, and timestamps. When a review is deleted, a snapshot is created with the deleted_at timestamp. This ensures full auditability for platform compliance and customer dispute resolution.

A review is only eligible for creation after an order has been delivered, as enforced by business rules. The review cannot be modified or deleted if the associated product has been deleted or if the seller account has been suspended.

This endpoint supports the snapshot principle by returning all historical states of a review, allowing administrators to reconstruct the exact state of a review at any point in time for regulatory compliance, fraud investigation, or evidence in customer disputes.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the customer review to retrieve. This UUID corresponds to the id field in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

responseBody.description: The review data with its complete historical snapshot history.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Create a new product review from an authenticated customer.

This endpoint allows registered customers to submit reviews for products they have purchased and received. Reviews can only be created for order items that have been delivered (status 'delivered'), as verified by the system through the shopping_mall_order_items relationship. A customer may submit only one review per order item due to the unique constraint on shopping_mall_order_item_id in the database schema.

The review includes a required rating (1-5) and an optional text field for detailed feedback. All reviews are associated with the exact product and variant as they existed at the time of purchase, preserving historical accuracy for dispute resolution. Once created, reviews cannot contain the same order item identifier twice.

This endpoint is authenticated: only customers may create reviews for products they have purchased. Review creation may only occur after delivery confirmation, ensuring reviews are based on actual product experience.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate the authenticated customer has a corresponding order item with status 'delivered'. 
- Retrieve the shopping_mall_order_item_id from the request body
- Verify the order item exists and is associated with the authenticated customer
- Confirm the order item status is 'delivered'
- Check that no existing review exists for this order item (unique constraint enforcement)
- Create a new shopping_mall_reviews record with the provided rating and optional text
- Set created_at to current timestamp
- Set shopping_mall_product_id and shopping_mall_customer_id from the order item
- Return the newly created review object with full details including id, created_at, and all submitted data

requestBody.description: Data required to create a new product review.

responseBody.description: The created review object with all details including system-generated fields.

operations.specification:
When a review is deleted, the system must:
1. Verify the review exists and is owned by the requesting customer
2. Check that review is not already deleted (deleted_at is null)
3. Copy the current state of the review into the shopping_mall_review_snapshots table with version = current + 1
4. Update the shopping_mall_reviews table to set deleted_at to current timestamp and updated_at to null
5. Return 204 No Content on success
6. Return 404 Not Found if review doesn't exist or is already deleted
7. Return 403 Forbidden if user is not the review owner
8. The operation must occur within a single database transaction to ensure data integrity
operations.description:
Permanently remove a customer review from the database.

This operation permanently deletes a customer review from the shopping_mall_reviews table. Unlike systems that preserve deleted records for audit purposes, this platform performs hard deletion of reviews that are removed by customers. There are no soft delete mechanisms or preserved historical copies of reviews in this system.

The operation is only available to the customer who originally wrote the review. Administrators can view but cannot delete reviews through this endpoint. After deletion, the review is permanently removed from all customer-facing interfaces including product detail pages, review lists, and search results. The review content, rating, and associated metadata are no longer accessible through any API endpoint.

This operation affects the product's average rating calculation, removing the review's contribution from all statistical computations. There is no recovery mechanism available for deleted reviews.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: UUID identifier of the review to delete. Must be a valid UUID that corresponds to an existing review in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

operations.name: erase

operations.description:
Submit or update a customer's vote on a specific review.

This endpoint allows an authenticated customer to cast a vote indicating whether they found a review helpful or not. Each customer can vote only once per review, as enforced by a unique constraint on the combination of review_id and customer_id. If a vote exists for this customer-review pair, it will be updated with the new value. Otherwise, a new vote record will be created. The vote type must be either 'helpful' or 'not_helpful'.

The operation is idempotent. The review must exist and be active (not marked as permanently deleted). If the review does not exist or has been permanently deleted, the system returns '404 Not Found'. For any authorization failure (including unauthenticated requests), the system returns '403 Forbidden'.

This operation has no dependencies on other APIs and relies on the review having been previously created through a valid order delivery process.
operations.name: vote
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting customer is authenticated and has the associated review as part of their order history.
Find the review by reviewId and verify it is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).
Verify the review's shopping_mall_order_item_id links to a completed order item belonging to the authenticated customer.
If an existing vote by this customer for this review exists, overwrite its vote_type field with the new value.
If no vote exists, create a new record in shopping_mall_review_votes with the customer_id, review_id, vote_type, and timestamps.
Use a transaction to ensure atomicity.
Return HTTP 204 No Content on success.
Return 403 if customer is not authorized to vote on this review.
Return 404 if review does not exist or is deleted.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review to vote on. Must correspond to an existing review record.
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: The type of vote to submit: 'helpful' or 'not_helpful'. Must be one of these two values.

operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_review_votes table by id field to retrieve single vote record.
Validate that reviewId corresponds to the record's shopping_mall_review_id.
Return vote_type, created_at, and updated_at fields.
Return 404 if vote not found or if reviewId does not match the vote's review association.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific customer vote on a product review.

This operation returns the exact type of vote (helpful or not_helpful) cast by a customer on a particular product review. Each vote is uniquely identified by both the review ID and the vote ID, ensuring precise access to individual feedback interactions.

The vote record includes the vote type and timestamps indicating when it was created and last updated. Since votes are immutable once cast, the updated_at field will typically equal created_at. This endpoint provides direct access to community feedback data, enabling review quality assessment and filtering of helpful content.

This operation is part of the review ecosystem where customers can rate the usefulness of other customers' reviews. The data returned here helps surface high-quality reviews and improves the review experience by highlighting valuable feedback from the community.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review being voted on. Must correspond to a valid shopping_mall_reviews record.

parameters.name: voteId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the specific vote record. Must correspond to a valid shopping_mall_review_votes record.

responseBody.description: The specific vote record, including type and timestamps.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete historical snapshot history of a specific review.

This endpoint provides full audit access to all preserved states of a review, ensuring complete transparency for dispute resolution, compliance, and customer trust. Every edit or deletion of a review creates an immutable snapshot that preserves the review's rating, text, actor, and timestamps exactly as they existed at that moment.

The returned data includes every version of the review from its initial creation through all subsequent edits and final deletions. Each snapshot contains the actor's identity, which allows verification of who made each change. This endpoint is critical for enforcing the platform's snapshot principle that every business-relevant state change must be permanently recorded.

Access to this endpoint is strictly limited to the customer who created the review and platform administrators. Regular users can only view their own review histories. Administrators may access any review's snapshot history for dispute resolution or compliance purposes.

This API operation requires no request parameters beyond the review ID, since all historical data is stored within the shopping_mall_review_snapshots table. The system automatically orders snapshots chronologically by created_at timestamp for consistent viewing.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_review_snapshots table for all records matching the review_id parameter. Join with shopping_mall_customers to retrieve actor display name. Order results by created_at ascending to show chronological history. Apply pagination with limit and offset. Filter results to include only snapshots belonging to the specified review. Return error if review does not exist. Include count of total snapshots in response metadata.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the review whose snapshot history is being requested.
parameters.name: reviewId

responseBody.description: Paginated list of all historical snapshots for the specified review, including rating, text, actor, timestamps, and snapshot metadata.

operations.description:
Update an existing customer review for a product. This operation allows a customer to modify their previously submitted review by changing the rating (1-5) or the optional written text. All changes create an immutable snapshot of the prior version in the review_snapshots table to preserve the historical state for dispute resolution and audit purposes. Review edits are permitted only for reviews with active status, and cannot change the review's association to product, order, or customer. Modifications are not permitted after a review has been deleted. The updated review reflects the changes immediately, but the original review data remains accessible through its snapshot history.

The update is restricted to customers who authored the review. Admins have no direct write access to reviews via this endpoint. All modifications are captured by the snapshot system, ensuring verifiable audit trails for content changes. This operation does not allow changing the review's product, customer, or order association, as these relationships are immutable once established.

After update, the system automatically generates a review snapshot with the prior state. The updated review's updated_at timestamp is refreshed, and the new version is immediately visible to all users. The previous version remains available for audit through the snapshot endpoint. This ensures both current accessibility and historical integrity simultaneously.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update an existing review by ID. First, validate the provided reviewId exists and belongs to the authenticated customer. Check that the review has not been deleted (deleted_at is null). Load the current review record. Extract new rating and/or text values from the request body. Validate that rating is between 1 and 5 if provided. Validate text length is between 0 and 500 characters if provided. Create a review snapshot with the current state of the review before update. Update the review record with new rating and/or text values. Set updated_at timestamp to current time. Return the updated review object with new values. Log the update event in system_audit if enabled.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to update. This UUID references the shopping_mall_reviews.id field.
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Fields that can be updated in the review: rating and text. Rating must be an integer between 1 and 5. Text must be a string with maximum 500 characters.

responseBody.description: The updated review record after changes have been applied, including the new rating and/or text, and the updated_at timestamp.

operations.specification:
Insert a new shopping_mall_review_votes record with provided shopping_mall_review_id, shopping_mall_customer_id, and vote_type. Validate that:
1. reviewId references existing shopping_mall_reviews.id with deleted_at IS NULL
2. customer_id from authentication context matches the provided shopping_mall_customer_id
3. Vote does not already exist for this review-customer pair (enforces @@unique constraint)
4. vote_type is either 'helpful' or 'not_helpful'
5. Return generated record with id, created_at, updated_at
Use atomic transaction to prevent race conditions during creation.
operations.description:
Submit a helpful or not helpful vote on a specific review.

This endpoint allows authenticated customers to vote on the usefulness of review content to help surface valuable feedback across the marketplace. Each customer may cast exactly one vote per review, as enforced by the unique constraint on (review_id, customer_id).

The vote type must be explicitly specified as either 'helpful' or 'not_helpful'. The customer's identity is derived from the authenticated session; it is not included in the request body.

Voting is not subject to time limits, and the vote cannot be changed once submitted — customers must submit a new vote if their assessment changes (which will be recorded as a separate record).

Note: This endpoint is only accessible to authenticated customers.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: The UUID of the review being voted on. Must reference an existing shopping_mall_reviews record that is not logically deleted.

requestBody.description: The type of vote to cast: 'helpful' or 'not_helpful'.

responseBody.description: The newly created vote record with system-generated identifiers and timestamps.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: A review must be created before it can be voted on, as votes require an existing review record to reference.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific system log entry by its unique identifier. This endpoint provides access to immutable audit records that capture critical system events such as snapshot generation failures, payment gateway errors, and maintenance activities. All system logs are generated automatically by the platform infrastructure and are preserved permanently for operational transparency and regulatory compliance.

The log entry includes the event type, severity level, timestamp, and optional structured JSON metadata containing diagnostic information such as error stack traces, request IDs, and server identifiers. This endpoint enables administrators to investigate system incidents, verify recovery actions, and generate compliance documentation.

System logs are append-only and cannot be modified, deleted, or overwritten. Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrators due to the sensitive nature of diagnostic information that may contain internal system details.

This operation requires the logId to be a valid UUID. Attempts to request a non-existent log will return a 404 error. The metadata field, if present, will be returned as a JSON string and may contain nested context about the event.

Dependencies: 
- This operation does not depend on any other API operations.
- System logs are generated independently of user actions and cannot be influenced by other endpoints.
- Administrative access to this endpoint is governed by the platform's permission hierarchy.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the shopping_mall_system_logs table with the provided logId (UUID) using a simple WHERE clause. Return the full record including id, created_at, event_type, severity, and metadata fields exactly as stored. Return 404 Not Found if no log entry exists with the provided ID. Return 500 Internal Server Error if database connection fails. Metadata field is returned as a JSON string and should be serialized as-is without parsing or transforming.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the system log entry. Must be a valid UUID format.
parameters.name: logId

responseBody.description: System log entry containing detailed information about a platform event.

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_system_logs table with advanced filtering options. Implement cursor-based pagination for large datasets. Support filtering by event_type (exact match) and severity level (exact match). Support range queries on created_at timestamp (gte, lte). Join with metadata fields for string searching in JSON field using full-text search. Return summary fields only: id, created_at, event_type, severity, and metadata length. Apply strict authorization: only admin actors may call this endpoint. Use database index on (created_at, severity) for performance optimization.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filtered history of system-level events from the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint provides administrators with access to the immutable audit trail of infrastructure events, including snapshot generation failures, payment gateway errors, maintenance mode activations, and other systemic exceptions. The system logs capture critical operational events with detailed contextual metadata to enable comprehensive incident response and forensic analysis.

Administrators can search across event types such as "snapshot_generation_failure", "payment_gateway_timeout", or "maintenance_mode_enabled" with precise severity filtering (info, warning, error, critical) and timestamp range queries. The query engine leverages full-text search capabilities on the metadata JSON field for diagnostic pattern matching.

All results return a summary view optimized for performance and display. This endpoint supports pagination via cursor-based pagination to handle large volumes of log data without performance degradation. Access is restricted to authenticated administrators only. Each log entry is immutable and permanently retained to satisfy regulatory compliance and forensic auditing requirements.

This operation depends on the administrative oversight capability defined in 11-administrator-system.md. For comprehensive system diagnostics, it should be used in conjunction with the user-facing order and product history endpoints.

requestBody.description: Advanced search criteria for system log records with filtering, range, and text query options.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of system log summary records for operational monitoring and forensic analysis.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_admin_actions table by id field matching the URL path parameter actionId. Return the complete record including admin_id, action_type, affected_entity_type, affected_entity_id, reason, and created_at fields. Ensure the id parameter is validated as UUID format before database lookup. Return 404 if no record found with the specified UUID. No transactions, joins, or complex logic required - single row retrieval with UUID validation.
operations.description:
Retrieve the complete audit record of a specific administrative action performed on the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint provides detailed visibility into all platform governance actions, including administrator approvals, rejections, suspensions, and other overrides. Each entry in the audit trail captures the full context of the action: which administrator performed it, what entity was affected (seller, product, order, customer, or category), the specific reason for the action, and the exact timestamp of when it occurred.

This data is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_actions table, which maintains an unchangeable audit log where all records are permanently preserved and cannot be altered or deleted under any circumstances, in accordance with the platform's snapshot principle.

All audit records are generated by the system and reflect actions performed by administrators as defined in the shopping_mall_admin_actions schema. No data in this table is ever modified or removed after creation.

The response includes key metadata for each action: the administrator who performed the action, the type of action performed, the entity affected, and the timestamp of the action. This enables administrators to trace platform governance decisions and verify compliance with platform policies.

This endpoint is critical for maintaining an immutable audit trail as required for regulatory compliance and platform sustainability. All data returned represents the definitive historical record of administrative actions on the platform.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete, immutable historical snapshot of any system entity (product, variant, seller profile, review, etc.) as it existed at a specific point in time.

This endpoint provides forensic-level audit trail access for dispute resolution, compliance reporting, and platform integrity verification. Every change to the system — whether product edits, seller profile updates, review modifications, or cancellation/refund requests — creates a permanently preserved snapshot that captures the entity's complete state before and after the modification.

When you request a snapshot by its unique ID, you receive the unaltered, raw JSON representation of the entity's state exactly as it was captured at the time of the event. This includes all field values, relationships, and metadata. For edits, the snapshot_data contains both "before" and "after" states. For deletions, it captures the final state before removal. This provides an irrefutable record of what was visible to users, what prices were listed, and what seller profiles looked like when transactions occurred.

This access is critical for:
- Resolving customer disputes about product specifications or pricing
- Verifying seller identity during order fulfillment
- Auditing administrative actions
- Meeting regulatory compliance requirements (GDPR, PCI-DSS)
- Recovering data from accidental modifications

All snapshot data is stored in write-once immutable storage and cannot be modified or deleted, even by administrators. This ensures the integrity of the platform's historical record.

This operation retrieves the full snapshot object directly from the shopping_mall_snapshots table. No other API endpoint provides access to this level of historical detail. Any modification attempts to the snapshot data will be blocked by the system.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_snapshots table by snapshotId. Return the entire snapshot_data JSON object exactly as stored in the database. No filtering, transformation, or aggregation. Return 404 if snapshotId does not exist. Ensure read-only access with no side effects. The snapshot_data field contains a fully serializable JSON object representing the exact state of the entity at time of capture, including all fields and relationships.

parameters.description: Unique identifier for the snapshot record to retrieve. This UUID corresponds to the id field in the shopping_mall_snapshots table.
parameters.name: snapshotId

responseBody.description: The complete, unmodified snapshot data as stored in the database. Contains a serialized JSON object representing the exact state of the entity (product, variant, seller, review, etc.) at the time the snapshot was created. For edits, includes both "before" and "after" states. For deletions, includes the state before removal.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filtered list of immutable snapshot records from the audit trail.

This operation supports comprehensive search and filtering capabilities across the system's historical data, enabling administrators and compliance officers to reconstruct the state of products, variants, seller profiles, reviews, and requests at any point in time. This is essential for dispute resolution, regulatory audits, and forensic investigations.

Users can filter snapshots by entity type (product, variant, seller_profile, review, cancellation_request, refund_request), actor (customer, seller, or admin), action type (created, edited, deleted, approved, rejected), and time period. The response includes only essential summary information for performance optimization when displaying large lists.

Snapshots are never modified or deleted in this system, so this read-only operation presents an immutable historical record. For complete fidelity, the full snapshot state can be retrieved using IShoppingMallSnapshot.id via a separate GET operation.

This endpoint is critical for maintaining the platform's commitment to immutable records and forensic-level audit trails outlined in 12-snapshot-principle.md.

Join with actor tables to enrich actor_type and actor_id with names where needed. Use materialized views for performance on large datasets. Retrieve the global configuration settings for the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint returns the complete set of operational parameters that govern the entire e-commerce marketplace system. These settings include commission rates, subscription fees, approval timeouts, content constraints, and other platform-wide business rules that are configured exclusively by administrators.

The settings are immutable from customer-facing interfaces and are designed for system-wide consistency. Every transaction, approval process, content constraint, and automated workflow in the platform adheres to these configuration values. This data is critical for administrative dashboards, compliance audits, and system monitoring tools that require visibility into the operating parameters of the marketplace.

While customers and sellers operate within these constraints, this endpoint is intended for administrative use only. The values are not meant to be modified by end users and reflect the platform's governing business policies. All calculations, validations, and automation rules throughout the system derive their thresholds and limits from these stored settings.

This endpoint does not require any parameters since the system settings represent a singleton configuration record. The response includes every configurable parameter in the platform, maintaining a complete picture of the system's behavioral constraints at any point in time.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific immutable snapshot of a seller's profile (shop name, description, logo) as it existed at a point in time.

This operation returns the exact state of a seller's shop identity—including name, description, and logo—at the moment a snapshot was captured, typically triggered by a profile edit. This historical record is critical for dispute resolution, audit compliance, and verifying the seller's identity at the time of purchase or review. Every snapshot is permanently preserved and cannot be altered, ensuring an unchangeable audit trail.

Only the seller who modified their profile or a system administrator can access this snapshot. Customers may access snapshots indirectly via their order history or reviews, but this endpoint exposes only the snapshot data itself—not ownership context, which must be derived from related records like order items.

The snapshot is a fixed point in time: it does not reflect current seller information, and no live profile fields are exposed through this endpoint.To resolve disputes, this snapshot serves as the authoritative record of what the seller's identity appeared to be during any transaction or interaction.

This endpoint is part of a system-wide snapshot architecture that ensures trustworthiness and legal compliance across all business-critical state changes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Perform a direct lookup on the shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots table using the snapshotId as the primary key (UUID). Return the record with fields: name, description, logo_url, created_at. If no record is found, return 404 Not Found. Do not join with sellers, orders, or reviews—this endpoint must return only the snapshot data exactly as stored. No caching permitted—always serve from the immutable storage layer. Transactional integrity is ensured by database-level read consistency. No authentication logic in service layer—authorization is handled by API gateway based on JWT claims.

responseBody.description: The immutable snapshot of a seller profile captured at a specific point in time, containing name, description, logo URL, and creation timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated inventory analytics across the entire platform for administrative oversight.

This operation provides a comprehensive view of inventory trends across all seller products, including total stock levels by category, cumulative sales volume over a specified period, restock frequency, and out-of-stock rates. The data is summarized to prevent exposure of sensitive seller or customer details while enabling strategic inventory planning at the platform level.

The analysis can be filtered by date range, category, seller, or product name, allowing administrators to drill down into specific product segments. Results are returned in paginated format to handle large datasets efficiently.

This endpoint supports reporting, supply chain forecasting, and fraud detection. All data is derived from immutable inventory_histories and product_variants records, ensuring accuracy even if seller profiles or product details have changed since the original sales.

For performance, the system pre-aggregates daily inventory statistics in materialized views to enable sub-second response times on large datasets. The endpoint never returns individual variant or order data — only aggregated summaries.

This operation does NOT allow modification of inventory. It is strictly for viewing and analysis purposes only.

Filter by date range, category, seller_id, or product_name if provided in request.

Include product count per category.
Order results by total_stock descending, then by category_name.
Return cursor-based pagination using after_key from request or first page if omitted.
Use materialized view for high volume.
Apply admin-only permission check: only users with role 'admin' can access.

The response includes total units sold, current stock levels, average price per variant, and the number of unique sellers offering each variant. All metrics are computed from immutable order item and inventory history records to preserve the historical truth of each transaction even if product details or prices change over time.

The operation supports filtering by date range and pagination for large result sets. This endpoint should be used exclusively by administrators for strategic planning, inventory forecasting, and financial analysis.
