operations.name: index

operations.description:
Check the status of email verification for a user account.

This endpoint validates an email verification token provided via the URL path and determines whether it corresponds to an active verification record for either a customer or seller account. The system maintains separate verification records for customers and sellers, each with their own immutable audit trail.

When a user registers, a unique verification token is generated and sent to their email address. This endpoint allows the user to verify their account by including the token in the URL path, checking whether it is still valid (not expired, not deleted) and which type of account it corresponds to. The verification record is retained indefinitely in an immutable state for compliance purposes, even after successful verification.

For customer accounts, the token is issued during registration and expires after a set period (usually 24 hours). For seller accounts, the token serves the same purpose but is linked to an application that requires administrative approval before full access is granted.

The response indicates whether a valid verification record exists, and if so, whether it belongs to a customer or seller account. The response does not return sensitive data like email addresses or personal information, maintaining user privacy while providing the necessary status information.

This service is critical for account security and compliance, ensuring that only verified users can access their accounts and preventing fraudulent registrations. Verification records are immutable and permanently preserved in the database, providing an audit trail for security and legal requirements.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table for matching token where deleted_at is null and expires_at > current timestamp.
If found, return {type: 'customer', status: 'valid'}.
If not found, query shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications table for matching token where deleted_at is null and expires_at > current timestamp.
If found, return {type: 'seller', status: 'valid'}.
If neither found, return {type: null, status: 'invalid'}.
Ensure the token parameter is validated as a string with appropriate length and format (alphanumeric, URL-safe).
Never return customer or seller email addresses or other personal data.
All verification records are immutable and must remain unchanged in database.

parameters.description: Verifiable token received from the email verification link. Must be a URL-safe, 64-character alphanumeric string.
parameters.name: token

responseBody.description: Response containing the type of account being verified and its verification status.

operations.description:
Initiate a password reset request for either customer or seller accounts.

This operation allows an authenticated or unauthenticated user to initiate a password reset process by providing their registered email address. Upon receipt, the system generates a temporary reset token with a 1-hour expiration and stores it in the corresponding password reset table (shopping_mall_customer_password_resets or shopping_mall_seller_password_resets). The system does not return the reset token to the client for security reasons. Instead, a confirmation token ID is returned for audit purposes.

The operation is accessible to both customer and seller actors. Upon successful request, the user will receive a password reset email containing a time-limited link. The token viability is strictly enforced at 60 minutes — no extensions or renewals are permitted. Multiple requests can be initiated with the same email, but the system automatically invalidates prior tokens upon new request creation.

This endpoint is intentionally designed without user ID routing to prevent account enumeration. Attackers cannot determine valid user accounts by testing ID paths because email is the sole identifier. This conforms to OWASP security recommendations and the platform's commitment to privacy-first design.

This operation has no effect on the user’s current session. They remain logged in unless explicitly logged out. Only when the reset link is activated does a new session token get issued. No cookies or authentication headers are accepted in this request, as it is designed to function even when the user lacks active credentials.

This endpoint MUST NOT be confused with account creation, login, or authentication. It is purely a password recovery mechanism. It is not intended for verification or account recovery beyond password reset.

Failure conditions:
- If the email is not registered: returns 200 OK for security reason (prevents enumeration)
- If email format is invalid: returns 400 Bad Request
- If rate limiting is exceeded: returns 429 Too Many Requests
- Internal failure: returns 500 Internal Server Error
operations.name: request
operations.specification:
Generate a verifiable unique token ID (UUID) and use it as the primary key for the password reset record.

Look up the account (customer or seller) by provided email in respective tables (shopping_mall_customers or shopping_mall_sellers).

If no account found: create a dummy reset record with a valid token ID, but do not send email — still return 200 OK as defensive security practice.

If account found:
- Invalidate any existing reset tokens for this email in the respective password reset table
- Insert a new reset token record with: token_id, email, user_id (customer_id or seller_id), issued_at (now), expires_at (now + 60 minutes), used: false
- Send password reset email via configured SMTP system with link: https://shoppingmall.com/reset?token={token_id}

Return response with token_id to enable audit trail and user-facing confirmation.

All token generation and email sending must be done in a single transaction with retry logic for email delivery on failure.

Store request method, IP address, user agent (if available), and timestamp in system_logs for behavioral analysis.

Do NOT return the raw token string in the response. Only return the token_id. This prevents token leakage.

Use JSON schema for input validation before processing: email must be valid RFC 5322 email format.

Use indexing and locking on password reset tables to prevent race conditions during concurrent requests.

Restrict POST rate limit to 5 requests per email per hour across all clients. Perform this check before ever querying the database.

Use quarantine buckets for suspicious requests (e.g., repeated invalid emails or malformed payloads).

requestBody.description: Password reset initiation request containing the user's email address and optional expiration settings.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of password reset request with a unique audit token ID. Does NOT contain the actual reset token for security.

Return response with token_id to enable audit trail and user-facing confirmation.

All token generation and email sending must be done in a single transaction with retry logic for email delivery on failure.

Store request method, IP address, user agent (if available), and timestamp in system_logs for behavioral analysis.

Do NOT return the raw token string in the response. Only return the token_id. This prevents token leakage.

Use JSON schema for input validation before processing: email must be valid RFC 5322 email format.

Use indexing and locking on password reset tables to prevent race conditions during concurrent requests.

Restrict POST rate limit to 5 requests per email per hour across all clients. Perform this check before ever querying the database.

Use quarantine buckets for suspicious requests (e.g., repeated invalid emails or malformed payloads).

operations.description:
Reset a user's password using a valid reset token issued during password recovery.

This endpoint allows a user to change their password after successfully validating a password reset token received via email. The operation requires the user to provide the reset token and a new password. The system validates the token against the corresponding password reset record (shopping_mall_admin_password_resets, shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, or shopping_mall_seller_password_resets) to ensure it is active, unexpired, and unmodified. Once validated, the user's password_hash is updated with the new bcrypt-hashed password, the associated reset record is marked as used or deleted, and the user's session is invalidated to ensure security.

This is not a generic update endpoint—it is strictly for password recovery and must only be accessible after a token has been issued. No new password can be set without a valid, unexpired, unvalidated token. The operation follows the transactional pattern where password update and reset token invalidation occur atomically. Authorization is handled by existing JWT session tokens, which must be present in the Authorization header during this request.

Field validation rules:
- password must be minimum 8 characters, containing letters and numbers
- length under 128 characters
- token must match exactly with an active reset record
- the token must not have been used before
- user must be authenticated (Bearer JWT token)

This endpoint does not allow password reset for deleted accounts.

Related operations: GET /password-reset (request token), POST /login (authenticate after reset)

operations.description:
Retrieve the active authentication sessions for the currently authenticated actor (customer, seller, or admin).

This endpoint provides a comprehensive view of the user's active login sessions across their respective actor type. The system resolves the actor type automatically from the session token (JWT) and queries only the appropriate session table (shopping_mall_admin_sessions, shopping_mall_customer_sessions, or shopping_mall_seller_sessions). This ensures strict actor isolation and security compliance by preventing cross-type session enumeration.

Each returned session represents a single authentication event, capturing connection context including IP address, referrer, and timestamps. Sessions are immutable audit records - they are created upon login and become invalid upon expiration, logout, or account suspension. Deleting or modifying sessions is not permitted; they are preserved permanently for security auditing.

The response includes session properties common across actor types: creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, IP address, referrer, and the absolute URL (href) of the page where login occurred. The response structure preserves actor context to prevent ambiguity: the actor type is embedded in the response schema through the leading prefix "shopping_mall_" in the table name context.

This endpoint is not used for troubleshooting sessions or initiating logout - to terminate a session, use platform logout functionality, which revokes the refresh token and invalidates the session at the protocol level.
operations.name: get
operations.specification: Detect actor type from JWT payload (admin, customer, or seller). Query corresponding session table: shopping_mall_admin_sessions, shopping_mall_customer_sessions, or shopping_mall_seller_sessions. Filter results by actor_id from JWT. Order by created_at descending to show most recent sessions first. Ensure no cross-actor data leakage. Return minimum list of session properties: id, created_at, expired_at, ip, href, referrer, and actor type identifier. Attach actor type as metadata field without exposing internal table names.

responseBody.description: Array of active authentication sessions for the authenticated actor

operations.description:
Terminate an active session by invalidating its JWT tokens and marking it as inactive.

This endpoint implements session termination for both admin and customer authentication sessions. According to the system's audit trails design, all session records are immutable and append-only. This operation does not delete the session record but instead sets the is_active flag to false to indicate that the session has been terminated.

This pattern ensures that all authentication events are permanently preserved for security auditing, compliance, and forensic analysis. The actual JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) are not stored for future validation but are immediately invalidated with this operation.

The system maintains separate session tables for admin and customer actors, but both follow the same audit pattern: session ID is a UUID, a created_at timestamp is recorded, and the session is terminated by setting is_active to false when logout occurs or tokens expire. This endpoint allows users to manually terminate their sessions before automatic expiration.

The session identified by sessionId must exist in either the shopping_mall_admin_sessions or shopping_mall_customer_sessions tables, as these are the only session entities maintained by the system. Attempting to terminate a non-existent session will return a 404 error.

Note: This operation leaves the session record intact for historical audit purposes. The session is logically deleted (soft delete) by the is_active flag and cannot be restored.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Look up the session record with the provided sessionId in either shopping_mall_admin_sessions or shopping_mall_customer_sessions tables. If found, update the is_active field to false. This is an atomic operation that does not change any other fields (to preserve audit integrity). Return a 204 No Content response on success. If the session ID does not exist in either table, return a 404 Not Found response. Never delete the record physically - only set is_active=false to comply with the immutable audit trail principle.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the session to terminate. Must be a UUID that exists in either shopping_mall_admin_sessions or shopping_mall_customer_sessions table.
parameters.name: sessionId

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to calculate total transaction amounts. Use cursor-based pagination to support large result sets. Filter by status field (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially_completed) and created_at date range. Join with shopping_mall_customers to include customer information in summaries. Exclude deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL). Calculate total amount from order_items sum. Apply indexing to status, created_at, and customer_id for performance optimization.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of completed sales transactions.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities across the shoppingMall platform's order history, allowing users to filter sales by status, customer, and date range. The response includes summarized sales information optimized for dashboard displays and high-performance browsing of transaction records.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting. The operation uses advanced filtering to quickly narrow down large datasets of orders by their status and timeframe. The response consists of summarized data rather than full order details, reducing network overhead and improving loading times for list views.

Because the platform uses an immutable snapshot architecture, all sales data referenced is the exact state at time of purchase, ensuring accurate historical reporting and compliance with financial regulations. Orders with status 'partially_completed' contain mixed transaction statuses and should be reviewed manually. The system implements soft delete for orders: records with deleted_at not null are preserved for audit purposes but are excluded from regular queries.

All order data in the response is derived from shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables with their respective snapshots in shopping_mall_snapshots for historical accuracy.

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive administrative dashboard with aggregated platform metrics.

This endpoint provides administrators with a real-time overview of the shoppingMall platform's operational status, enabling effective oversight and informed decision-making. The dashboard displays essential statistics across all core domains of the platform, including seller activity, order volume, product distribution, and system health metrics.

The data presented is derived from immutable snapshot records and represents the authoritative state of the platform. The statistics reflect the entire platform ecosystem and are computed from the complete history of transactions, approvals, suspensions, and system events. This ensures administrators can make decisions based on verified, unchangeable historical data rather than volatile or manipulable real-time data. The dashboard does not allow modifications - all administrative actions must be performed through dedicated endpoints (e.g., force-cancel, force-refund, approve-seller).

System administrators use this dashboard as their primary interface for platform management, monitoring for anomalies, identifying trends, and ensuring platform integrity. The aggregated metrics enable rapid identification of systemic issues such as sudden drops in seller approvals, spikes in cancellation requests, or abnormal inventory adjustments.

The dashboard includes data from all administrator actions recorded in the shopping_mall_admin_actions table, seller statuses from the shopping_malls_sellers table, order statuses from the shopping_mall_orders table, product listings from the shopping_mall_products table, and system-level events from the shopping_mall_system_logs table. All data is presented in summary form to avoid overwhelming administrators with raw data while still providing comprehensive insights.

The response includes a timestamp of when the summary data was last computed, ensuring administrators know the recency of the information they are reviewing. This timestamp is based on the system's processing time, not the current wall-clock time, maintaining consistency with the platform's immutable data model.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query admin_actions, sellers, orders, products, and system_logs tables to compute aggregated metrics.
- Count total administrators (active and inactive)
- Count total sellers by status: approved, rejected, suspended, pending
- Count total orders by status: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially completed
- Count total products with active variants
- Count total pending cancellation requests
- Count total pending refund requests
- Count total system logs from the last 24 hours
- Compute total transaction volume (sum of all order totals)
- Compute average order value
- Compute seller approval rate (approved / total applications)
- Compute customer retention rate based on repeat order data
- Compute inventory turnover rate
- Return all metrics in a single summary object with timestamp of computation.
- All data must be derived from immutable snapshots, not live tables.
- Return only the summary object with no pagination, as this is a single summary endpoint.

responseBody.description: Summary statistics for platform administration dashboard.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of order statuses for the authenticated customer.

This endpoint provides a high-level overview of all orders placed by the authenticated customer, showing the current status of each order as derived from its constituent order items. The status reflects the aggregate state of all items within an order, which can be 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded', or 'partially completed'.

This API is designed for customer order history views where users need to quickly assess the status of their orders without loading detailed item information. The response includes only essential summary data to optimize performance for listing views.

For detailed information about specific orders, including items, shipping, and pricing, customers should use the GET /orders/{orderId} endpoint.

The status value is calculated server-side by aggregating the statuses of all order items according to the business rules defined in the shopping_mall_orders model, ensuring consistency across all client applications. All data reflects the state at the time of the request.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_orders table filtered by customer_id from authenticated session. Apply pagination with default 10 records per page and support cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Order results by created_at in descending order (newest first). Extract only the following fields: id, order_number, status, created_at. Include total count of matching orders in response metadata. Return IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary type as response structure.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order status summaries containing order number, status, and creation timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated revenue statistics for the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint provides comprehensive revenue reporting for administrators, calculating total commission income from all completed transactions. Revenue is derived from the 7.5% commission rate applied to each order's total value, as defined in the business model. All financial calculations are based on immutable order item snapshots stored in the database, ensuring that revenue figures reflect the exact pricing, discounts, and product states at time of purchase, not current values.

The system maintains immutable financial records so that administrators can generate accurate reports that cannot be manipulated by changes to product prices, seller profiles, or discount policies after the fact. Each order item's unit_price and quantity are captured from the cart snapshot at checkout, forming a legally defensible audit trail for financial reporting.

This endpoint supports administrative functions including financial auditing, investor reporting, tax compliance, and platform profitability analysis. All revenue data is tied to the same immutable snapshot architecture that preserves product, variant, and seller states at time of transaction.

Related operations:
- The data returned by this endpoint is based on the order_items table, which is populated through the checkout process described in 07-order-management.md
- The commission calculation (7.5%) is defined in 03-business-model.md and applied as a system rule
- No direct interaction with inventory or cart data occurs - revenue is derived solely from completed order items with status 'delivered'
- The results must be accurate regardless of subsequent changes to products or sellers, relying entirely on snapshot data

Error handling:
- If no orders exist within the requested period, returns an empty data array with pagination
- Invalid date formats return 400 Bad Request with specific field errors
- Non-admin actors receive 403 Forbidden response
- Database connection issues return 500 Internal Server Error with appropriate logs.

Business context:
- All financial calculations are based on the exact state preserved in order_item snapshots
- The system does not adjust revenue figures retroactively if a seller's commission rate changes
- Revenue tracking is independent of seller suspension or account deletion - historical revenue remains intact
- No direct API interaction with user accounts or product listings affects this data

Security requirements:
- Only admin actors can access this endpoint
- All results are read-only - immutable snapshot data cannot be modified
- All access attempts are logged in shopping_mall_admin_actions
- Response data should never be cached for more than 1 hour to prevent stale reporting

Data integrity:
- Revenue calculation: sum(order_item.quantity * order_item.unit_price * commission_rate)
- Commission rate is fixed at 0.075 (7.5%) as defined in shopping_mall_system_settings
- All calculations are performed using precise decimal arithmetic to avoid rounding errors
- Results must match the exact amounts recorded in the system's financial audit trails
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_order_items table for order items with status 'delivered'. Join with shopping_mall_orders to filter by order creation date range. Calculate total revenue by summing (quantity * unit_price * 0.075) for all matching order items. Apply optional seller_id filter if provided. Return results with pagination using cursor-based strategy to handle large datasets efficiently. Use SQL window functions to calculate totals for each page without full table scans. Cache result for 30 minutes but refresh immediately if admin requests fresh data. Log access via shopping_mall_admin_actions with action_type: 'retrieve', affected_entity_type: 'revenue'. Use read replicas for reporting queries to avoid impacting transactional database performance.

requestBody.description: Filtering parameters for revenue reporting

responseBody.description: Paginated revenue summary statistics

operations.description:
Update a shipment record's status in a controlled manner according to platform business rules.

This endpoint allows only specific status transitions for shipment records as defined by the shoppingMall platform's immutable audit principle. When a customer receives their order, they may confirm delivery, which triggers a status change from 'shipped' to 'delivered'. The system will also automatically change the status to 'auto-delivered' after 14 days if delivery has not been confirmed by the customer. This endpoint is designed to maintain a verifiable, unchangeable audit trail for all delivery events.

No other status transitions are permitted. Attempting to set the status to 'shipped' on an already shipped record (or any other unauthorized state change) will result in an error. The system strictly enforces that shipment status can only progress forward and cannot be reverted or set to arbitrary values. The carrier and tracking number information may be updated once to ensure accuracy of delivery tracking, but any subsequent changes to tracking details must create a new shipment record rather than modifying the existing one.

This operation works in conjunction with the order item status transitions. When a shipment's status changes to 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered', the system automatically updates the associated order items' status to 'delivered' as well. This ensures full consistency between the physical delivery record and the digital order status.

The endpoint is protected to prevent unauthorized access - only customers who placed the order or system-level processes can initiate status updates. This design reinforces the platform's foundational principle that all commercial transactions must leave an immutable, verifiable audit trail that cannot be manipulated retroactively.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Accept shipmentId from path parameter. Validate that shipmentId exists and is associated with a valid shipment record. Check current shipment status - only allow status update from 'shipped' to 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered'. Validate that status parameter is one of the allowed values: 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered'. If status is 'delivered', record confirmation metadata including timestamp, IP address, and device information. If status is 'auto-delivered', verify that 14 days have passed since shipment creation. Update the shipment record with new status and any provided tracking information. Ensure the carrier name and tracking number are provided and valid (alphanumeric, 8-32 characters). Validate that the tracking number is unique and properly formatted. Update the associated order items' status to match the new shipment status. Log all status transitions in the immutable audit trail. Return the updated shipment record with current status and timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment to be updated. Must match exactly with the shopping_mall_shipments.id field.
parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: Parameters to update the shipment record with new status and tracking information.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record with the new status and timestamps.

operations.specification:
Validate that the shipment exists and is owned by the authenticated customer.
Retrieve shipment record by shipmentId and verify the associated order item belongs to the customer's account.
Ensure shipment status is currently 'shipped' - reject if already 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered'.
Update shipment status to 'delivered' with current timestamp.
Update the associated order item's status from 'shipped' to 'delivered'.
Record the customer confirmation event in system_logs with IP, device, and timestamp.
Trigger any associated business logic: enable review submission, initiate refund eligibility window.
Return the updated shipment record with new status.
operations.description:
Confirm delivery of a shipment to complete the order fulfillment cycle.

This endpoint allows a customer to formally confirm receipt of their ordered items. Once confirmed, the shipment status transitions from "shipped" to "delivered", which triggers several downstream business processes including enabling product review submission, initiating the 7-day refund eligibility window, and potentially activating loyalty or rewards programs.

This confirmation is critical for maintaining data integrity in the platform's immutable audit trail. The system does not permit multiple delivery confirmations for the same shipment, and once confirmed, the delivery status becomes permanently locked. The customer can confirm delivery via a mobile app, web interface, or automated system notification.

For security and privacy, this operation verifies that the authenticated customer owns the specific shipment being confirmed. The system matches the customer's authenticated account with the order item associated to the shipment, preventing unauthorized delivery confirmations. The confirmation event itself is permanently recorded with customer device signature, IP address, and exact timestamp for dispute resolution and legal compliance.

This operation is directly related to the POST /shipments endpoint, where sellers create shipment records, and the PATCH /shipments/{shipmentId}/tracking endpoint, where tracking information is updated. This confirmation operation represents the final step in the fulfillment workflow.

When a customer does not confirm delivery within 14 days, the system automatically performs this confirmation on their behalf, as defined in the automatic delivery policy. This customer-initiated confirmation takes precedence over any automatic confirmation. Once a manual confirmation occurs, automatic delivery will be canceled for that shipment.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record after successful delivery confirmation, including the new status and confirmation timestamp.

For administrators, this endpoint provides oversight capability to monitor all customer cancellation requests across the platform, enabling timely intervention when necessary.

operations.description:
Retrieve all refund requests initiated by the authenticated customer.

This endpoint returns a complete list of all refund requests created by the current authenticated customer, providing full visibility into refund history including pending, approved, and rejected requests. Each refund request represents a customer's formal request to reverse payment for a specific order item, typically due to product dissatisfaction or delivery issues.

The response includes the full refund request details: reason provided by the customer, current status (pending/approved/rejected), creation and update timestamps, and auto-approval deadline. This enables customers to track the status of their refund requests and understand expected resolution timelines.

For audit and dispute resolution, this endpoint provides complete historical visibility into all refund activity. The refund requests are tied to specific order items, preserving the exact product, variant, price, and seller information as it existed at time of purchase. All refund request records are permanently preserved in the system with no deletion capability.

This operation is read-only and does not alter any data. The permanent record ensures compliance with financial and consumer protection regulations requiring immutable audit trails.

This endpoint provides sellers with a unified view of all unresolved customer claims requiring their attention, combining both cancellation requests (for paid but unshipped items) and refund requests (for delivered items) into a single interface. The response includes the request type, customer information, reason for the request, creation timestamp, and any associated seller response.

Security: Only the seller who owns the products associated with these requests can access this information. The endpoint automatically filters requests based on the authentication context, ensuring sellers can only see requests for their own products.

Business context: This endpoint is critical for seller dispute resolution workflows. Sellers have a time-limited window (48 hours for cancellations, 72 hours for refunds) to respond to these requests before automatic approval occurs. This dashboard provides the primary interface through which sellers manage these time-sensitive business decisions.

Related operations:
- POST /seller/requests/{requestId}/respond - Submit response to a pending request (follow-up operation)
- GET /seller/requests/history - View historical responses to completed requests
- GET /customer/requests/pending - View customer's own pending requests

This endpoint does NOT include requests that have been completed (approved or rejected) or requests for products owned by other sellers.

The operation returns both cancellation requests (for paid-but-not-shipped order items) and refund requests (for delivered order items) in a single unified list with pagination, enabling administrators to efficiently manage and resolve customer disputes.

The response includes essential metadata for each request: request type (cancellation or refund), request ID, current status (pending), creation timestamp, associated customer information, and a preview of the customer's reason for the request. Full request details are not included in this summary to maintain performance and security; administrators can access detailed information by drilling down into individual requests using the provided request IDs.

This endpoint supports filtering by status, created_at date range, customer_id, and seller_id to help administrators prioritize their workload. The system enforces that cancellation requests automatically approve after 48 hours and refund requests after 72 hours if no seller response occurs, so this endpoint primarily shows pending requests requiring administrative attention.

This operation is accessible only to users with admin privileges as defined by authorizationActor: "admin".

This endpoint complements the GET /admin/sellers, GET /admin/products, and GET /admin/orders endpoints, providing the request management component of the complete administrative oversight system.

This endpoint returns the complete set of global configuration parameters that govern business rules across the entire platform. These settings include commission rates, premium subscription fees, automatic approval timeouts, product and image limits, and other operational parameters that are managed exclusively by administrators.

The returned configuration is immutable from the client's perspective and represents the authoritative state of platform-wide business rules that affect all users, sellers, and system processes. Any changes to these settings require administrator access through backend interfaces, not through this API endpoint.

This configuration is used by all platform components, including the authentication system, order processing engine, inventory management, and content moderation systems, to ensure consistent policy enforcement across the entire marketplace.

operations.description:
Retrieve immutable audit trail records from the shopping_mall_snapshots table.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive historical audit trail of all significant changes made to platform entities including products, variants, seller profiles, reviews, and administrative actions. Every change to the system is permanently recorded as an immutable snapshot to ensure integrity for compliance and dispute resolution.

The audit trail captures exact state changes for: entity modifications, seller actions, customer reviews, and administrator interventions. Each record contains the full before-and-after state of the entity at the moment of change, along with the actor responsible and precise timestamp.

This functionality is critical for regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PCI-DSS), forensic investigations, and resolving business disputes where historical accuracy is paramount. Administrators can reconstruct exactly how a product appeared, what a seller's profile looked like, or how a review was modified at any point in time.

The endpoint supports filtering by entity type (product, variant, seller_profile, review, cancellation_request, refund_request), actor ID, time range, and action type (created, edited, deleted, approved, rejected, canceled, refunded). Results are sorted in descending chronological order and use cursor-based pagination to handle potentially large audit volumes efficiently.

This endpoint is read-only and no modifications to the audit records are permitted under any circumstances.

This operation provides a comprehensive overview of system health by aggregating system_events according to the selected criteria. The returned dashboard data includes counts of events by event_type and severity_level, distribution over time, and identification of critical incident patterns.

The system-logs table records immutable infrastructure events such as snapshot generation failures, payment gateway timeouts, and maintenance mode activations. All entries are automatically generated by the system and cannot be modified or deleted by users. This endpoint only provides read-only access to monitoring data.

Administrators use this dashboard to proactively detect system anomalies, investigate incidents, and validate operational stability. The data is not for transactional purposes but for forensic analysis and preventative maintenance.

Key security consideration: Only authenticated admin actors may access this endpoint. It provides no sensitive user data but may expose internal system architecture through event types.

This operation requires no pre-execution of other APIs. However, for comprehensive monitoring, this dashboard should be reviewed alongside the admin_actions table for correlating system events with administrative interventions.

Retrieve a comprehensive, paginated audit trail of all administrative actions performed on the shoppingMall platform.

This report provides a complete historical record of governance activities, including seller approvals and rejections, account suspensions and bans, product and order overrides, and category modifications. Every action is recorded with immutable details including the administrator who took the action, the affected entity, the reason for intervention, and the precise timestamp.

This endpoint is critical for platform compliance, dispute resolution, and governance transparency. Administrators use this report to verify compliance with regulatory requirements, resolve customer disputes with authoritative evidence, and audit internal procedures. Each entry preserves the exact business state at time of action, enabling forensic reconstruction of platform events.

The report supports advanced filtering by administrative action type (approve, reject, suspend, ban, override), affected entity type (seller, product, order, customer, category), time period, and administrator. Results are paginated for performance with large datasets.

This endpoint leverages the platform's unique snapshot architecture, where every administrative action is permanently recorded with full context. The data shown represents unalterable records, providing the highest assurance for legal and compliance purposes.

Related operations: GET /admin-actions/{id} to view the complete snapshot of a single administrative action, and GET /admin-actions/snapshot/{snapshotId} to view the immutable snapshot content itself.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete immutable history of a seller's profile changes.

This endpoint returns a chronological list of all snapshot records of a seller's shop name, description, and logo as they appeared at the time of each change. This history is critical for platform administrators to audit changes and for dispute resolution. Each snapshot captures the exact state of the seller's profile at the moment it was edited, ensuring that historical representations of the seller are permanently preserved.

According to the platform's mandatory snapshot principle (12-snapshot-principle.md), all profile modifications are recorded as immutable snapshots in the shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots table. These records are never deleted, modified, or overwritten.

This operation is accessible only to administrators, as indicated by the /admin/ path segment. The returned snapshots are ordered from most recent (newest) to oldest. Each snapshot contains only the data as it existed at that point in time — not the current state. Even if a seller updates their name or logo today, all previous snapshots remain unchanged and accurately reflect how the seller appeared during past transactions.

This endpoint does not return the current profile (which is not stored in shopping_mall_seller_profiles due to violation of the snapshot principle) — only historical snapshots.

Do not join with other tables; snapshots are self-contained.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for authentication sessions across all actor types (admin, customer, seller). This structure enables comprehensive audit trail queries by administrators for security monitoring and compliance checks. The query applies to all session records across the platform, enabling filtering by actor type, date ranges, active status, and IP address to identify suspicious activity or audit specific time periods. Pagination allows navigating large result sets efficiently.

Use this object to specify which sessions to retrieve from the system's complete audit log of authentication activity. Only administrative users can access this endpoint. Filters are applied to session metadata fields only - no authentication tokens or sensitive credentials are exposed in the response.

All date/time fields must be in ISO 8601 format. Pagination parameters follow standard conventions used throughout the API.
IShoppingMallAdminSession.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Implements search criteria for auditing all actor sessions (admin/customer/seller). Must accept: actor_type filter (required), created_at range, expired_at range, is_active status, IP address, plus pagination parameters. This request object is used to query the UNION of shopping_mall_admin_sessions, shopping_mall_customer_sessions, and shopping_mall_seller_sessions.

Filtering: 
- actor_type: must match one of 'admin', 'customer', 'seller'
- created_at_from/to: ISO 8601 format (datetime), inclusive range
- expired_at_from/to: ISO 8601 format (datetime), inclusive range
- is_active: true/false
- ip: partial text match (case-insensitive substring)

Pagination: 
- page: integer >= 1, default 1
- limit: integer 1-100, default 25
- sort_field: 'created_at' (only allowed value)
- sort_order: 'asc' or 'desc', default 'desc'

Always return only summary fields (id, actor_type, created_at, etc.) as per operation specification. Must never attempt to retrieve private authentication data.

This schema defines only search parameters, not the response structure. This object is used for querying the union of session tables from the database, never for direct table mapping.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh.description: Request for exchanging a valid refresh token for a new set of authentication tokens. Contains a single refresh_token string that was previously issued during seller login or refresh. This token has a 30-day lifetime and enables seamless session continuation without requiring re-authentication with email and password. Used exclusively by sellers to renew their short-lived access tokens. Never includes user profile, password, or session metadata.
IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Validates the refresh_token against the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. Confirms the token has not expired (expires_at > current time), has not been revoked (session not marked deleted), and is associated with a non-deleted, approved seller account. If valid, generates a new access_token (30-minute TTL) and a new refresh_token (30-day TTL), then invalidates the old session by marking it as deleted in shopping_mall_seller_sessions. The seller's approval status and email verification are not re-validated because they are guaranteed by the existence and validity of the refresh token itself, which is only issued after successful login with a confirmed and approved account.

IShoppingMallCustomer.description: Complete customer entity representing a registered user of the shoppingMall platform. Includes all public profile information accessible after authentication. This schema is used in responses to retrieve customer details. For security, sensitive fields like password_hash are excluded. Session and verification data are managed through separate endpoints and not included here to maintain separation of concerns.
IShoppingMallCustomer.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_customers database table. All properties are direct column values with no computation or transformation. The entity represents a customer account with public profile information accessible after authentication. Sensitive fields like password_hash are explicitly excluded. deleted_at is nullable to represent account inactivation; null = active, timestamp = inactive.

IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate.description: Complete representation of a product with updated fields for modification. IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products table. IShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary of a cart item, displaying only essential information needed for the customer's shopping cart interface. This includes the product name, seller shop name, variant options (e.g., size, color), variant price, quantity, and timestamp of cart addition - all captured as immutable snapshots at the time of cart addition. This ensures pricing and product representation accuracy for checkout, even if the underlying product or seller details have been modified since the item was added to the cart. Excludes full descriptions, logos, and deletion status for efficient UI rendering.
IShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Summary representation of a cart item, exposing only the immutable snapshot data captured at the time of cart addition for display in the customer's shopping cart interface. All fields are sourced directly from the shopping_mall_cart_items table without computation or derivation.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.description:
Authentication session data including security tokens and connection metadata for audit purposes.

This DTO represents a complete authentication session record returned by the system when querying session details by sessionId. The session data includes essential security information for auditing and verification purposes, including access and refresh tokens, client IP address, referrer URL, and session expiration timing.

Session records are immutable and maintained for forensic analysis. This view provides a complete snapshot of the authentication event as it occurred, including the client's connection context. The data is used for security investigations, compliance audits, and authentication validation.

Note: No token regeneration or modification is possible through this endpoint. This represents a read-only view of historical authentication data.
IShoppingMallCustomerSession.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping of shopping_mall_customer_sessions table fields: id, access_token, refresh_token, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, is_active. IShoppingMallProductImage.description: A list of product images in their new display order after reordering. This list reflects the exact state of the images after the reorder operation and can be used to update the UI with correct visualization order.

Each image object includes all database columns: id (UUID), product_id (UUID), url (image storage path), sort_order (display sequence), created_at (timestamp), width (pixels), height (pixels). This DTO is returned after the PUT /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/images operation and represents the exact state of the image collection immediately after reordering. The sort_order values form a continuous sequence starting at 0. All values are copied directly from the database with no transformation. Note: file_size and file_type were previously incorrectly included but do not exist in the database schema.

IShoppingMallProductInventorySummary.description: Summary of inventory status for a single product variant, showing current stock level and variant details as they were at the time of the most recent inventory change. Used to display product availability in inventory reports.

No filtering, no pagination - pagination handled by parent IPage type.

IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.description: Request payload containing authentication credentials for seller login. Includes email address and plain-text password. The server will validate the email against the shopping_mall_sellers table, verify the password using BCrypt comparison with the stored password_hash, and check that the seller's approval_status is 'approved'. No profile or session data is included. This is a pure authentication request.
IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: This schema defines the authentication request payload for seller login. The server performs a single-query lookup on shopping_mall_sellers using the provided email and then verifies the password hash. The seller's approval_status must be 'approved' according to business logic, but this is not part of the schema structure — it's handled in the service layer. Any other fields in the request body cause validation failure.

IShoppingMallSeller.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: This schema defines the request payload for seller account registration. No validation of order_item_id existence required in DTO - system validates during processing

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Search request parameters for filtering and paginating product listings.

This object defines the query criteria for retrieving products based on textual search terms, price ranges, and timestamp ranges. Customers and administrators use this to discover products matching specific criteria within the marketplace.

The name and description fields support partial text matching using trigram similarity for flexible searching. The base_price fields allow filtering products within a price range. The created_at and updated_at fields enable date range filtering to find recently added or modified products. The page and limit parameters control pagination of results.

All filter fields are optional; omitting a field means that dimension is not used for filtering. This allows users to search by any combination of criteria without requiring all fields to be specified.
IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Processes search query against shopping_mall_products table. Filters by: name (trigram similarity), description (trigram similarity), base_price (between min/max), created_at (between min/max), updated_at (between min/max). Implements pagination with offset (page - 1) * limit and limit. Joins with shopping_mall_product_variants implicitly to ensure only products with available variants are returned. Does not filter by deleted_at as the API already excludes deleted products. Values are case-sensitive for exact matching, case-insensitive for pattern matching via trigram. All fields are optional; if not provided, that filter is ignored.

IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.description: Request body for confirming delivery of a shipment. Contains the delivery status ('delivered' or 'auto-delivered') and an optional reason provided by the customer. Used to trigger the final step of order fulfillment and initiate inventory restore.

IShoppingMallAdminAction.description:
Complete administrative action record with full context of the action performed.

This entity represents an immutable audit record of governance actions performed on the shoppingMall platform, including administrator approvals, rejections, suspensions, bans, and other overrides. Each record captures the full context of the action: which administrator performed it, what type of entity was affected (seller, product, order, customer, or category), the specific reason for the action, and the exact timestamp of when it occurred.

Access to this information is critical for compliance, dispute resolution, and platform integrity. Administrators can use this record to review historical decisions, verify that proper procedures were followed, and understand the context behind any platform action that affected users or data. The immutable nature of these records ensures that every administrative intervention is permanently traceable for legal and regulatory purposes, in accordance with the platform's snapshot principle.

All audit records are generated by the system and reflect actions performed by administrators as defined in the shopping_mall_admin_actions schema. No data in this table is ever modified or removed after creation.

No joins, aggregations, or transformations required - single row query by UUID. Always returns complete record for audit integrity. All data is immutable, permanently preserved, and cannot be altered or deleted under any circumstances in accordance with the platform's snapshot principle.

IShoppingMallAdminAction.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Aggregates data from shopping_mall_inventory_histories and shopping_mall_product_variants. Computes total_restocks: sum of all positive inventory changes (restocks, adjustments). Computes out_of_stock_rate: (count of variants with stock = 0) / (total variants in category) * 100. Computes product_count: count of distinct products in category with at least one variant. Does not reference any single row — entirely computed from audit trails.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ISummar.x-autobe-specification: This summary DTO represents the cancellation request context for UI display. All data is derived from the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table with additional lookups to shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_sellers to retrieve product_name, variant_sku, and shop_name. This is a read-only display schema that does not accept input and excludes sensitive internal IDs (order_item_id, customer_id, seller_id) that are derived from JWT tokens. The schema provides a complete business context of a cancellation request without exposing system-level identifiers.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh.description: JWT refresh token used to renew access tokens in the authentication system. This value is issued during customer login and must be securely stored client-side. When presented to the refresh endpoint, the system validates it against the session record and issues new access and refresh tokens if validation succeeds.
IShoppingMallCustomer.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: This is a simple token submission DTO for token refresh operation. The refresh_token field contains a JWT string that was previously issued during customer login or join. The system validates this token by looking up its SHA-256 hash in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. The token must be valid (not expired, not revoked) for the refresh operation to succeed. There are no other fields or metadata required for this operation.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description: Lightweight product summary for display in search results and category listings. Contains just the product name, price, creation timestamp, and a reference to the seller's summary profile, all essential for customer decision-making without overwhelming data.
IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_products table with relation to shopping_mall_sellers. Includes only essential summary fields for listing display and search results. Computed fields are excluded per design requirement to ensure minimal payload.

IShoppingMallOrder.description:
Complete order record with all order items and their comprehensive snapshots, preserving the exact state of products, variants, and seller profiles at time of purchase.

This object represents the full audit trail of a customer's order, preserving pricing, product descriptions, seller identity, and variant details as they existed at the exact moment of purchase. It is designed for legal compliance, dispute resolution, and customer transparency.

The order header displays immutable metadata including the unique order number, overall status derived from its items, total amount, and timestamps of creation and updates. Each order item contains a complete frozen state of the product purchased: the product name and description as displayed, the category assigned at time of purchase, the base price, and all product images as they appeared. The variant information includes the exact SKU code, option values (color, size, etc.), the unit price charged, and the available stock quantity at time of purchase. Seller information includes the shop name, description, and logo exactly as shown on the marketplace at the time of transaction to preserve reputation context.

This structure ensures absolute data integrity: even if the product is renamed, the variant is modified, or the seller changes their profile, the customer's order history always reflects the precise state of the marketplace at the moment of purchase. No live data is ever displayed. All information is derived from immutable snapshots stored in the system.

Note that sensitive information such as customer identity, payment details, and internal IDs are excluded. The entire response is read-only and designed for customer and administrator viewing, not for modification.
IShoppingMallOrder.x-autobe-specification: The IShoppingMallOrder is read-only and represents the full order record as retrieved from the shopping_mall_orders table via join with shopping_mall_order_items. It includes the order header fields (order_number, status, total_amount, created_at, updated_at) from shopping_mall_orders. The order_items property contains an array of objects, each representing an order item and containing the complete immutable snapshot data from shopping_mall_snapshots: product details (product_name, product_description, category_name, base_price, thumbnail_image, all_product_images), variant details (variant_sku, option_values, variant_price, stock_at_time_of_purchase), and seller details (shop_name, shop_description, logo_url). All snapshot fields are read from the snapshot table at time of query. The snapshot is embedded in-line, not referenced by ID. No references to IDs are exposed. All derived fields are calculated from stored snapshots during query execution.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate.description: Request body for uploading a product image. The image must be supplied as a binary file in multipart/form-data format. The server will generate all metadata including the storage URL, file dimensions, and sort order.
IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is for multipart/form-data upload request, not JSON body. The server receives binary image data and generates all fields: image_url (storage path), width, height (from image metadata), sort_order (max existing + 1), created_at (current timestamp), and links to product_id from path parameter. Client does not provide any of these values.

IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.description: Request parameters for filtering and paginating order history by status, date range, customer/seller, amount thresholds, sort order, and results per page. Accepts a comprehensive set of search criteria for order transaction data across the shoppingMall platform.
IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
The request schema defines advanced search parameters for querying the shopping_mall_orders table with exhaustive filtering capabilities for order status, date ranges, customer/seller IDs, total amount thresholds, sorting, and pagination.

- Available values for 'status': 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded'
- 'createdAtRange' must contain both 'start' and 'end' fields as ISO 8601 datetime strings
- 'customerId' and 'sellerId' must be UUID format strings
- 'totalAmount' must use comparison operators (> , < , >= , <= , between) with numeric values, never direct value setting
- 'sort' must be one of: 'created_at', 'total_amount', 'status'
- 'offset' allowed from 0 to infinity (default 0)
- 'limit' must be between 1 and 100 (default 10)

For customer requests, 'customerId' is automatically filtered via JWT token and should not be sent in the request.
For admin requests, all filters are active and must be explicitly provided.

The schema is used in both /shoppingMall/customer/orders (customer context) and /shoppingMall/admin/sales (admin context) endpoints.
Filters are combined with AND logic, and responses use offset/limit pagination with no cursor support since datasets are small (<10K records).

IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate.description: Request payload for updating the delivery status of a shipment. Only the status field is required to confirm delivery ('delivered') or trigger auto-delivery after 14 days ('auto-delivered'). Carrier name and tracking number may be optionally provided to correct initial tracking information, but cannot be changed after the initial shipment creation.
IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents a controlled state transition for shipment fulfillment. Only the status field is required and must be either 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered'. The carrier and tracking_number fields are optional and may be updated only once to correct initial inaccuracies. All other shipment data (product, variant, seller, timestamps) are immutable snapshots and cannot be altered. Status transition triggers automatic status update on associated order items via system logic.

IShoppingMallSnapshot.description: Immutable historical record capturing the complete state of any system entity at a specific point in time. Used for forensic audit, dispute resolution, and regulatory compliance. Contains the exact product description, price, variant options, seller profile, review content, or administrative action as it existed at the moment of change. The snapshot allows reconstructing the complete business context of any past transaction or modification with perfect fidelity.
IShoppingMallSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: Represents the snapshot_data field in shopping_mall_snapshots table. Contains serialized JSON object capturing the exact state of any system entity (product, variant, seller, review, etc.) at time of change. For create: {after: {entity_fields}}. For edit: {before: {previous_entity_fields}, after: {new_entity_fields}}. For delete: {before: {final_entity_fields}, after: {}}. Can contain any properties depending on the entity type. Must support nested objects, arrays, and primitive values. No fixed structure - schema must allow arbitrary JSON structure since it represents diverse entity states.

IShoppingMallRefundResponseSnapshot.description: Immutable record capturing the seller's decision and reasoning when responding to a customer-initiated refund request. This snapshot provides an unalterable audit trail of the seller's response, including their decision (approve or reject) and the precise reason provided, along with the exact timestamp of response. This record is used for dispute resolution, compliance audits, and fraud investigations, ensuring all actions are fully traceable and verifiable. Since this is an immutable historical record, the content cannot be modified after creation and represents the exact state of the seller's response at the time it was submitted.
IShoppingMallRefundResponseSnapshot.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_refund_response_snapshots table. This schema represents the immutable seller response record containing decision, reason, and timestamp. Each property corresponds exactly to a database column: decision (string), reason (string), responded_at (timestamp). This schema is used exclusively as the response body for PUT /shoppingMall/seller/refund-requests/{requestId}/response and reflects the actual structure of the database record.

IShoppingMallSnapshot.ISummary.description: A lightweight summary of an immutable snapshot record from the system audit trail. Used in paginated audit listings to provide essential metadata about system changes without including full snapshot data. Contains the unique identifier, type of entity changed, nature of action performed, timestamp, version number, and identifiers for both the actor who made the change and the target entity. Designed for efficient client-side display of audit histories and compliance reporting.
IShoppingMallSnapshot.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct projection of the shopping_mall_snapshots database table. This schema represents a lightweight summary used in paginated audit trail responses. All fields map directly to columns in the source table: id, entity_type, action_type, created_at, snapshot_version, actor_id, entity_id. Excludes snapshot_data, preceding_snapshot_id, updated_at, deleted_at to reduce payload size. actor_id and entity_id are stored as UUID strings (format: uuid) to ensure consistent resource identification across the API, per platform standard. No transformation or computation is involved — this is a direct read-only projection of immutable audit metadata.

email.description: User's registered email address for password recovery. Used to initiate the reset process without exposing account existence for security.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct API input that is used to look up customer or seller account in shopping_mall_customers or shopping_mall_sellers tables. Must be a valid RFC 5322 email format for system validation.

IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.description: Submit your registered email address to receive a time-limited password reset link. This is the only information required to initiate account recovery. For security, no other fields are accepted.
IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.x-autobe-specification: API input wrapper for initiating password reset via email. Validates RFC 5322 email format and triggers password reset flow in shopping_mall_customer_password_resets or shopping_mall_seller_password_resets tables. Does not store data directly but is the primary trigger for reset token generation and email notification.

IShoppingMallSnapshot.IResetResponse.description: Unique audit identifier for the password reset request. This token_id is used by the system to validate and process password reset requests securely. A client is never shown the actual reset token string for security reasons.
IShoppingMallSnapshot.IResetResponse.x-autobe-specification: The token_id field maps to the 'token' column in the shopping_mall_admin_password_resets table. This column stores the unique UUID generated during password reset request creation. The actual token string is never exposed to the client in any response; instead, this audit-safe token_id is used by the system to look up and process reset requests securely.

IShoppingMallSnapshot.IResetRequest.description: Request to initiate password reset by providing a user's registered email address. The system will not disclose whether the email exists for security reasons. Must be a valid RFC 5322 email address.
IShoppingMallSnapshot.IResetRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents a password reset initiation request. Must validate email format (RFC 5322) before any database lookup. Must initiate rate-limiting check (5 requests per email/hour) before querying shopping_mall_customers or shopping_mall_sellers. Must create a dummy reset record even if email doesn't exist, to prevent account enumeration. Must generate a unique token_id for audit logging. Must not expose whether account exists. Must be processed in a single transaction with email delivery retry.

scenario.draft:
Verify that the inventory summary endpoint correctly returns aggregated stock levels for all variants of a product with multiple product variants, each having distinct SKU codes and option values. The response should include accurate current stock calculations (sum of quantity_change from inventory_histories) for each variant, along with proper pagination metadata based on the request parameters. This tests the core business logic of inventory aggregation and pagination.

Validation points:
- The data array contains exactly one entry per variant of the product
- Each variant entry includes correct sku and option_values from product_variants table
- Each variant's current_stock accurately reflects sum of all inventory_histories quantity_change values
- Pagination metadata (current, limit, records, pages) correctly reflects the actual number of variants
- No variants from other products appear in results
- All inventory calculations are derived from immutable history records, not live stock values

functions.name: test_api_product_inventory_summary_multiple_variants

scenario.draft:
Verify that the inventory summary endpoint correctly returns an empty data array with valid pagination when a product has zero inventory across all its variants. This tests edge cases where all product variants have stock levels of zero, and ensures the system correctly calculates inventory by summing negative and positive inventory history records to arrive at zero, rather than failing or returning incorrect data.

Validation points:
- The data array is empty (length 0)
- Pagination metadata is still provided with current=1, limit=10, records=0, pages=0
- Product exists and has variants (verified in product_variants table)
- Inventory history records exist for the product variants but sum to zero
- No "out of stock" or error status is returned (inventory summary should be valid regardless of stock level)
- System correctly handles the case where all variants have neutral inventory (equal restocks and sales)
- System correctly handles negative inventory history records from past refunds with zero-positive net

This scenario ensures the system correctly handles edge cases where inventory summary returns no variants despite the product being active.

functions.name: test_api_product_inventory_summary_zero_inventory

scenario.draft:
Verify that the inventory summary endpoint correctly calculates the current stock for each product variant by accurately summing a complex sequence of inventory history records including restock, sale, return, and manual adjustment events. This tests the integrity and accuracy of the inventory calculation logic, ensuring the system correctly computes stock by aggregating all historical changes with proper signs (positive for restock, negative for sales/refunds).

Validation points:
- The data array contains exactly one entry for the variant
- The current_stock value equals: +100 (restock) + (-50) (sale) + 20 (return from refund) + (-5) (manual correction) = 65
- The variant has correct sku and option_values
- Pagination metadata is correctly formatted for single result
- Inventory history records are immutable and preserved (no direct stock field used)
- System correctly handles mixed positive and negative adjustments
- System correctly maintains historical context without allowing "live" stock updates

This scenario validates that the inventory calculation logic is mathematically accurate and properly implements the business rule that current stock = sum of all inventory_histories.quantity_change for each variant.

scenario.draft:
A registered customer uses a valid, verified email address to initiate a password reset. This triggers the system to generate a unique token ID, store it in the shopping_mall_customer_password_resets table with a 60-minute expiration, invalidate any existing reset tokens for that email, send a password reset email containing the token link, and return a 200 OK response with the token ID. The token must be cryptographically unique, stored securely, and not exposed in any other form. The system must not send an email if the customer has not yet verified their email address, but must still return 200 OK to maintain security posture.

Validation points:
- Response status is 200 OK
- Token ID is a valid UUID
- Token record exists with expires_at = now + 60 minutes
- Previous tokens for this email are marked used=true
- Email is sent to the registered email address with correct reset link
- User's current session is unchanged (no logout)
- No password, user ID, or token string is returned in response body

import { IEntity } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IEntity";
import { IPage } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IPage";
import { IPageIShoppingMallAdminSession } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IPageIShoppingMallAdminSession";
import { IShoppingMallAdminSession } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallAdminSession";
import { ArrayUtil } from "@nestia/e2e";
import { HttpException } from "@nestjs/common";
import { Prisma } from "@prisma/sdk";
import jwt from "jsonwebtoken";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";
import { v4 } from "uuid";

import { MyGlobal } from "../MyGlobal";
import { CustomerPayload } from "../decorators/payload/CustomerPayload";
import { PasswordUtil } from "../utils/PasswordUtil";
import { toISOStringSafe } from "../utils/toISOStringSafe";

export async function patchShoppingMallCustomerSessions(props: {
  customer: CustomerPayload;
  body: IShoppingMallAdminSession.IRequest;
}): Promise<IPageIShoppingMallAdminSession.ISummary> {
  const { page = 1, limit = 100 } = props.body as any;
  const offset = (page - 1) * limit;
  // Extract filter parameters
  const {
    actorType,
    createdAtStart,
    createdAtEnd,
    expiredAtStart,
    expiredAtEnd,
    isActive,
    ip,
  } = props.body as any;
  // Construct SQL UNION query for all session types
  const sql = `
    SELECT 
      id, 
      'admin' as actor_type, 
      admin_id as actor_id, 
      created_at::text as created_at, 
      expired_at::text as expired_at, 
      true as is_active, 
      ip, 
      href, 
      referrer
    FROM shopping_mall_admin_sessions
    WHERE ($1 IS NULL OR 'admin' = $1)
      AND ($2 IS NULL OR created_at >= $2::timestamp)
      AND ($3 IS NULL OR created_at <= $3::timestamp)
      AND ($4 IS NULL OR expired_at >= $4::timestamp)
      AND ($5 IS NULL OR expired_at <= $5::timestamp)
      AND ($7 IS NULL OR ip = $7)

    UNION ALL

    SELECT 
      id, 
      'customer' as actor_type, 
      shopping_mall_customer_id as actor_id, 
      created_at::text as created_at, 
      expired_at::text as expired_at, 
      is_active, 
      ip, 
      href, 
      referrer
    FROM shopping_mall_customer_sessions
    WHERE ($1 IS NULL OR 'customer' = $1)
      AND ($2 IS NULL OR created_at >= $2::timestamp)
      AND ($3 IS NULL OR created_at <= $3::timestamp)
      AND ($4 IS NULL OR expired_at >= $4::timestamp)
      AND ($5 IS NULL OR expired_at <= $5::timestamp)
      AND ($6 IS NULL OR is_active = $6)
      AND ($7 IS NULL OR ip = $7)

    UNION ALL

    SELECT 
      id, 
      'seller' as actor_type, 
      shopping_mall_seller_id as actor_id, 
      created_at::text as created_at, 
      expired_at::text as expired_at, 
      true as is_active, 
      ip, 
      href, 
      referrer
    FROM shopping_mall_seller_sessions
    WHERE ($1 IS NULL OR 'seller' = $1)
      AND ($2 IS NULL OR created_at >= $2::timestamp)
      AND ($3 IS NULL OR created_at <= $3::timestamp)
      AND ($4 IS NULL OR expired_at >= $4::timestamp)
      AND ($5 IS NULL OR expired_at <= $5::timestamp)
      AND ($7 IS NULL OR ip = $7)

    ORDER BY created_at DESC
    OFFSET $8
    LIMIT $9
  `;
  // Execute query with parameters
  const results: any[] = await MyGlobal.prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(
    sql,
    actorType,
    createdAtStart,
    createdAtEnd,
    expiredAtStart,
    expiredAtEnd,
    isActive,
    ip,
    offset,
    limit,
  );
  // Count total records for pagination
  const countSql = `
    SELECT COUNT(*) as total FROM (
      SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_admin_sessions
      WHERE ($1 IS NULL OR 'admin' = $1)
        AND ($2 IS NULL OR created_at >= $2::timestamp)
        AND ($3 IS NULL OR created_at <= $3::timestamp)
        AND ($4 IS NULL OR expired_at >= $4::timestamp)
        AND ($5 IS NULL OR expired_at <= $5::timestamp)
        AND ($7 IS NULL OR ip = $7)

      UNION ALL

      SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_customer_sessions
      WHERE ($1 IS NULL OR 'customer' = $1)
        AND ($2 IS NULL OR created_at >= $2::timestamp)
        AND ($3 IS NULL OR created_at <= $3::timestamp)
        AND ($4 IS NULL OR expired_at >= $4::timestamp)
        AND ($5 IS NULL OR expired_at <= $5::timestamp)
        AND ($6 IS NULL OR is_active = $6)
        AND ($7 IS NULL OR ip = $7)

      UNION ALL

      SELECT id FROM shopping_mall_seller_sessions
      WHERE ($1 IS NULL OR 'seller' = $1)
        AND ($2 IS NULL OR created_at >= $2::timestamp)
        AND ($3 IS NULL OR created_at <= $3::timestamp)
        AND ($4 IS NULL OR expired_at >= $4::timestamp)
        AND ($5 IS NULL OR expired_at <= $5::timestamp)
        AND ($7 IS NULL OR ip = $7)
    ) AS combined`;
  const countResult: any[] = await MyGlobal.prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(
    countSql,
    actorType,
    createdAtStart,
    createdAtEnd,
    expiredAtStart,
    expiredAtEnd,
    isActive,
    ip,
  );
  const total = countResult[0]?.total
    ? parseInt(countResult[0].total as string, 10)
    : 0;
  // Map results to IPageIShoppingMallAdminSession.ISummary format
  const data = results.map((row: any) => ({
    id: row.id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    actor_type: row.actor_type as "admin" | "customer" | "seller",
    actor_id: row.actor_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    created_at: row.created_at as string & tags.Format<"date-time">,
    expired_at: row.expired_at as string & tags.Format<"date-time">,
    is_active: row.is_active as boolean,
    ip: row.ip as string,
    href: row.href as string,
    referrer: row.referrer as string | null,
  }));
  return {
    data,
    pagination: {
      current: page,
      limit,
      records: total,
      pages: Math.ceil(total / limit),
    } satisfies IPage.IPagination,
  };
}
